In-scope processes.value: Annual Solvency UK hard close → Section A-E narrative drafting → QRT annex assembly → external audit of relevant elements → board approval → website publication and PRA notification, for the UK solo life and annuity entity

In-scope systems.value: Solvency UK balance sheet and own funds are consolidated in the close tool; narrative drafts and the audit trail sit in the financial reporting repository

checklist.step: Open the SFCR production plan and fix section ownership
actions: Create the <year> SFCR folder in the financial reporting repository and copy in last year's published Part 1 and Part 2 as the baseline.

Build the section ownership grid: A Business and Performance to the Financial Analyst, B System of Governance to the Corporate Secretary, C Risk Profile to the Enterprise Risk Manager, D Valuation for Solvency Purposes to the Valuation Actuary, E Capital Management to the Head of Capital Management.
Set the milestone dates back from the 14-week (70 business day) publication deadline: first draft at +40 business days, audit-ready draft at +50, board pack at +60.
Email each named owner the grid, their sub-headings from Reporting 3 and the PS3/24 Part 1 content list, and record their acceptance.
checklist.done: every Reporting 3 sub-heading has a named owner with an accepted draft date inside the 70-business-day window.

checklist.step: Lock the Solvency UK balance sheet that the narrative will quote
actions: Confirm the statutory hard close for 31 December is signed and take the Solvency UK valuation adjustments journal from the close tool.
Freeze the Solvency UK balance sheet version and record the version id — every narrative figure must cite that version.
Hand the frozen assets, technical provisions, own funds and SCR figures to the Valuation Actuary and the Head of Capital Management in a single dated pack.
Block further postings to the Solvency UK ledger scenario and notify the Senior Accountant that any late adjustment now needs CFO approval.
checklist.done: a single frozen, version-stamped Solvency UK balance sheet is issued to all section owners.

checklist.step: Draft Section A Business and Performance
actions: Write A.1 Business: legal name, PRA and FCA firm reference numbers, group structure chart, the external auditor's name, and the material lines of business (annuities and protection) and geographies.
Write A.2 Underwriting performance by Solvency UK line of business, taking premiums, claims and expenses from S.05.01 and explaining year-on-year movements over 10%.
Write A.3 Investment performance: income and gains by asset class from the investment accounting pack, plus gains/losses recognised directly in equity.
Write A.4 Performance of other activities including material leases, and A.5 Any other information.
Reference every figure to the frozen balance sheet version or the named QRT cell in the drafting comments.
checklist.done: Section A covers A.1-A.5 with every figure referenced to S.05.01 or the frozen balance sheet version.

checklist.step: Draft Section B System of Governance
actions: Pull the current board and committee terms of reference and the SMF responsibilities map from the board portal.

Write B.1 General governance (board and committee structure, material changes in the year), B.2 Fit and proper, B.3 Risk management system including the ORSA, B.4 Internal control system, B.5 Internal audit, B.6 Actuarial function, B.7 Outsourcing, B.8 Any other information.
State in B.3 the ORSA frequency, the date of the last board-approved ORSA and how ORSA output feeds capital planning, per Conditions Governing Business 3.
Confirm with the Chief Risk Officer and the Chief Audit Executive that B.3, B.4 and B.5 describe the functions as they actually operated in the year, and record their written confirmations.
checklist.done: Section B covers B.1-B.8 and the risk, internal audit and actuarial function descriptions carry written confirmations from their function heads.

checklist.step: Draft Section C Risk Profile
actions: Take the year-end risk register and the SCR risk-module split (S.25.01 or the internal model equivalent) as the spine for C.1 Underwriting, C.2 Market, C.3 Credit, C.4 Liquidity, C.5 Operational, C.6 Other material risks.
For each risk describe the measure used, the material exposures, the concentration and the mitigation, and state the stress and sensitivity results taken from the ORSA.
Disclose in C.4 the expected profit included in future premiums (EPIFP) figure calculated for own funds, as required for the liquidity risk disclosure.
Get the Chief Risk Officer to review the section against the board risk appetite statement and sign the review comment in the drafting file.
checklist.done: Section C covers C.1-C.6 with stress results, the EPIFP figure and a Chief Risk Officer review comment.

checklist.step: Draft Section D Valuation for Solvency Purposes
actions: Write D.1 Assets, D.2 Technical provisions, D.3 Other liabilities and D.4 Alternative valuation methods, each giving the basis, methods and main assumptions and a quantitative bridge to the IFRS financial statements.

In D.2 state the best estimate and risk margin separately by line of business from the Prophet run, the cost-of-capital rate used for the risk margin under the reformed Solvency UK basis, and the level of uncertainty.
Disclose the matching adjustment and volatility adjustment as applied, the portfolios they apply to, and the effect on technical provisions and own funds of setting each to zero.
Attach the model run reference and validation sign-off from the Model Risk Manager to each figure quoted.
checklist.done: Section D bridges Solvency UK to IFRS for assets, technical provisions and other liabilities, with matching-adjustment impacts quantified and model run references attached.

checklist.step: Draft Section E Capital Management
actions: Write E.1 Own funds: structure, amount and quality by tier, the capital management plan horizon, and a reconciliation of IFRS equity to excess of assets over liabilities and then to eligible own funds.
Write E.2 SCR and MCR giving the SCR by risk module, the MCR amount and its inputs, and the coverage ratios at the reference date and the prior year end.
Write E.3 (duration-based equity risk sub-module, if used), E.4 differences between the standard formula and any internal model, E.5 non-compliance with the MCR or SCR, and E.6 Any other information.
State explicitly whether the MCR or SCR was breached at any point in the year and, if so, the amount, duration and remedial action taken.
Tie every own funds and SCR figure to the S.23.01 and S.25.01 cells in the QRT annex.
checklist.done: Section E states own funds by tier, SCR and MCR coverage ratios, any breach in the year, and ties to S.23.01 and S.25.01.

checklist.step: Assemble the QRT annex for SFCR Part 2
actions: Take the annual QRT set submitted to the PRA and select the templates required for public disclosure: S.02.01 balance sheet, S.05.01 premiums claims and expenses by line of business, S.12.01 life technical provisions, S.22.01 long-term guarantee and transitional impact, S.23.01 own funds, S.25 series SCR and S.28 series MCR.
Export each template to the public disclosure layout and confirm the values are identical to the submitted instance, cell by cell, using the reconciliation macro.
Round and present in GBP thousands consistently and label the reporting currency and reference date on every template.
Hand the annex to the Statutory Reporting Manager with a signed statement that it matches the submitted return.
checklist.done: the public QRT annex is assembled and cell-for-cell identical to the templates submitted to the PRA.

checklist.step: Write SFCR Part 1 for the policyholder audience
actions: Draft the PS3/24 Part 1 document to the prescribed short structure: who the firm is, what it does, how financially secure it is, how it is run, and where to find Part 2.
Express the solvency position in plain terms (assets held against liabilities and the SCR coverage percentage) taking the figures only from the frozen Section E numbers — no new calculations.
Keep the document free of Solvency UK jargon; where a term such as 'Solvency Capital Requirement' must be used, define it in a sentence at first use.
Run a readability check and have the Head of Compliance confirm the document is not marketing material and makes no forward-looking promise.
checklist.done: Part 1 covers every PS3/24 required topic in plain English, uses only Section E figures, and carries Head of Compliance confirmation.

checklist.step: Tie the narrative figures back to the QRTs and the IFRS accounts
actions: Build a tie-out schedule listing every number that appears in Sections A-E with its source: QRT cell reference, frozen balance sheet line, or IFRS statement line.
Agree each own funds and SCR figure to S.23.01 and S.25.01, each technical provision to S.12.01, and each premium and claim figure to S.05.01.
Reconcile IFRS total equity to Solvency UK excess of assets over liabilities and show every reconciling item with an owner.
Raise a query to the drafting owner for any figure that cannot be traced, and hold the draft until it clears.
checklist.done: every quoted figure has a traced source on the tie-out schedule and the IFRS-to-Solvency UK bridge foots with no unexplained items.

checklist.step: Run the legal and compliance review over the disclosure
actions: Read Part 1 and Part 2 against the Reporting 3 sub-heading list and mark any required item that is missing or answered with a cross-reference only.
Assess any proposed non-disclosure of commercially sensitive information against the narrow grounds allowed in the Reporting Part, and require PRA approval evidence before accepting one.
Check that statements about litigation, group support and intra-group arrangements are consistent with the IFRS accounts and the legal matter register.
Record the review conclusion and any required changes as tracked comments on the draft.
checklist.done: counsel has confirmed every required sub-heading is addressed and any omission is supported by an approved non-disclosure basis.

checklist.step: Obtain the external auditor's report on the relevant elements
actions: Issue the audit-ready draft plus the tie-out schedule and the QRT annex to the external audit partner at the +50 business day milestone.
Answer audit queries on the relevant elements — the Valuation for Solvency Purposes and Capital Management sections and the associated templates — within 3 business days each.
Agree any audit adjustment with the Valuation Actuary and the Head of Capital Management, reissue the affected sections, and record the change on the tie-out schedule.
Collect the signed auditor's report on the relevant elements of the SFCR and file it with the draft.
checklist.done: a signed external auditor's report on the relevant elements is on file and all audit adjustments are reflected in the draft.

checklist.step: Take the SFCR to the board for approval
actions: Load Part 1, Part 2, the QRT annex, the auditor's report and the tie-out summary into the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting.
Include the proposed approval resolution confirming the board's responsibility for the SFCR and that the firm complied with the Reporting Part.
Minute the board's approval with the date, the attendees, the version approved and any conditions.
Circulate the signed minute to the Statutory Reporting Manager as the authority to publish.
checklist.done: the board has approved a named version of the SFCR and the signed minute is issued to the publisher.

checklist.step: Publish the SFCR and notify the PRA
actions: Publish Part 1 and Part 2 with the QRT annex on the firm's public website on a permanent, freely accessible page, and record the URL and the publication timestamp.
Confirm publication falls on or before the 14-week (70 business day) date after 31 December and capture the calendar proof.
Notify the PRA supervision contact of the publication date and URL by email, attaching the board approval minute reference.
Check the page from an unauthenticated browser session and confirm both PDFs open and are text-searchable.
checklist.done: both documents are live at a recorded public URL inside the 14-week deadline and the PRA has been notified in writing.

checklist.step: Archive the SFCR evidence pack under the retention rule
actions: Move the published PDFs, QRT annex, tie-out schedule, section owner confirmations, auditor's report, counsel review and board minute into the compliance evidence repository under REG-023/SFCR/<year>.
Apply the 10-year retention label from the publication date and set the record to legal-hold-eligible.
Index the record by reference date, entity, publication URL and board approval date so a PRA request can be answered without reassembly.
Confirm the prior-year record is still retrievable and has not aged out early.
checklist.done: the complete SFCR evidence pack is archived, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by reference date and entity.

testing.step: Build the population of required SFCR disclosure elements
actions: Extract every sub-heading required by PRA Rulebook Reporting 3 for Part 2 (A.1-A.5, B.1-B.8, C.1-C.6, D.1-D.4, E.1-E.6) and every content item PS3/24 requires in Part 1 into a requirement grid.
Add a row for each QRT required in the public annex (S.02.01, S.05.01, S.12.01, S.22.01, S.23.01, S.25 series, S.28 series).
Add a row for every quantitative figure quoted in the narrative, taken from the tie-out schedule.
Sign the grid as complete and record the Rulebook version date it was built from.
testing.done: the requirement grid holds one row per required sub-heading, template and quoted figure, dated to a stated Rulebook version.

testing.step: Reconcile the published document back to the board-approved version
actions: Download Part 1 and Part 2 from the public URL and compute a file hash for each.
Compare the hashes to the versions attached to the board approval minute in the board portal.
Where the hashes differ, obtain the change log and confirm each post-approval change was authorised by the Chief Financial Officer in writing.
Record any unauthorised post-approval change as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the published files match the board-approved versions, or every difference has written CFO authorisation.

testing.step: Draw and document the disclosure sample
actions: Take 100% of Section D and Section E rows because those are the externally audited relevant elements.
Take 30 further rows selected at random with a recorded seed from Sections A, B and C plus the quoted-figure rows, for a minimum of 60 rows in total.
Record the seed, the population size, the selection date and the grid version in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn.
Include every Part 1 content item in full — the population is small enough to test entirely.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all of Sections D and E and all of Part 1 is documented with its seed and population size.

testing.step: Re-perform the disclosure completeness assessment against the Rulebook
actions: Open PRA Rulebook Online at the Reporting Part as it stood at the reference date and read each sampled sub-heading requirement.
Locate the paragraph in the published SFCR that answers it and record the page and paragraph reference on the grid.
Judge sufficiency independently before reading the preparer's mapping; a cross-reference with no substantive content is a fail, not a partial.
Screenshot the Rulebook paragraph relied on into the workpaper for every failed or marginal row.
testing.done: each sampled requirement is mapped to a specific published paragraph or logged as not addressed, with a captured Rulebook source.

testing.step: Re-perform the narrative-to-QRT tie-out on the quoted figures
actions: For each sampled quoted figure, open the named QRT cell in the public annex and the corresponding cell in the instance submitted to the PRA.
Agree the narrative figure, the annex cell and the submitted cell to the pound thousand, and record all three values side by side.
Recompute the SCR and MCR coverage ratios from eligible own funds divided by the SCR and the MCR and compare to the published percentages.
Treat any difference over GBP 0.5m or 1% of the line as an exception regardless of the explanation offered.
testing.done: every sampled figure agrees across narrative, public annex and submitted instance, and coverage ratios recompute to the published values.

testing.step: Test the matching adjustment and technical provision disclosures in Section D
actions: Pull the Prophet run referenced in Section D and confirm the run id, the valuation date and the approval status of the run.

Recompute the disclosed effect of setting the matching adjustment to zero by taking the model's zero-MA sensitivity run and comparing the technical provision and own funds deltas to the published figures.
Agree the best estimate and risk margin split by line of business to S.12.01 and check the cost-of-capital rate stated in the narrative matches the rate applied in the run.
Record any unapproved or superseded model run supporting a published figure as an exception to the Chief Actuary.
testing.done: the disclosed matching-adjustment impact and technical provision split re-perform from an approved model run.

testing.step: Trace the governance assertions in Section B to primary evidence
actions: For each sampled B.1-B.8 assertion, locate the underlying evidence: terms of reference, SMF responsibilities map, ORSA board approval minute, internal audit charter, actuarial function report.
Confirm the ORSA date and frequency stated in B.3 match the board minute that approved the ORSA in the reporting year.
Confirm the outsourcing description in B.7 matches the material outsourcing entries on the outsourcing register at the reference date.
Log any assertion with no primary evidence as an exception naming the function head who confirmed it.
testing.done: each sampled governance assertion is supported by a dated primary document or is logged as unsupported.

testing.step: Recompute the publication deadline and test timeliness
actions: Recompute the deadline as 31 December of the reporting year plus 70 business days using the England and Wales business-day calendar, listing the holidays applied.
Compare the recomputed date to the recorded publication timestamp from the web server or content management log.
Confirm the auditor's report date and the board approval date both pre-date publication.
Any publication after the recomputed date, or approval after publication, is a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: the 70-business-day deadline is recomputed with a stated holiday calendar and publication is proven to fall on or before it.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception recording the sub-heading or figure, what was wrong and whether the published document is misleading.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: requirement grid out of date, section owner missed the milestone, figure changed after freeze, audit adjustment not carried through, deadline calendar wrong.
Name an owner and a remediation date, and for any misleading published figure open a PRA notification assessment with Regulatory Counsel the same day.
Carry every open issue into next year's SFCR test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue id, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the requirement grid and compare it to the zero-missing-sub-heading and zero-untied-figure thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer — who drafted no SFCR section and does not report to the Statutory Reporting Manager — sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any reportable breach to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an exception rate, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date is filed.

checklist.step: Fix the template scope for the reference date against the current PRA taxonomy
actions: Download the PRA Solvency UK taxonomy package and the accompanying template list for the reference date from the Bank of England regulatory reporting page.
Compare it to the prior submission scope and mark templates added, removed under PS15/24, or changed in structure.
Confirm which templates apply to the entity given it is a solo life and annuity firm using the matching adjustment, and record the applicability reason for each excluded template.
Issue the signed scope list to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and the Valuation Actuary before the data cut.
checklist.done: a signed, dated template scope list exists for the reference date with an applicability reason recorded against every excluded template.

checklist.step: Take the ledger data cut and reconcile it to the closed accounts
actions: Run the trial balance for the reference date from the general ledger after the close is signed, and export it at account and cost-centre level.
Apply the Solvency UK valuation adjustments journal and produce the assets, other liabilities and equity positions that feed S.02.01.
Reconcile the extracted totals to the signed statutory accounts line by line and clear every difference before release.
Release the dated extract to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst with the ledger version id stamped on it.
checklist.done: the ledger extract reconciles to the signed accounts with no unexplained differences and carries a version id.

checklist.step: Take the actuarial data cut for technical provisions
actions: Run the approved valuation model for the reference date and record the run id, model version and assumption set version.
Extract best estimate liabilities and risk margin by Solvency UK line of business for S.12.01, together with the matching adjustment portfolio split.
Produce the expected profits included in future premiums (EPIFP) figure using the prescribed method, for the own funds template.
Obtain the Model Risk Manager's validation sign-off on the run before releasing the extract, and attach it to the data pack.
checklist.done: technical provisions, the matching adjustment split and the EPIFP figure are extracted from a validated, version-stamped model run.

checklist.step: Load the source data into the reporting engine and clear mapping breaks
actions: Load the ledger extract, the actuarial extract and the investment holdings file into the reporting engine for the reference date.
Run the mapping report and list every source account or asset with no template destination, and every template cell with no source.
Resolve each break with the Controller or the Valuation Actuary and record the fix as a mapping change with an approver, never as a manual override on the template.
Re-run the load until the mapping report is clean and archive the final load log.
checklist.done: the load log shows zero unmapped source rows and zero unsourced template cells for the in-scope templates.

checklist.step: Produce the balance sheet and performance templates
actions: Generate S.02.01 balance sheet and check the Solvency UK value column against the ledger extract plus the valuation adjustments journal.
Generate S.05.01 premiums, claims and expenses by line of business and agree the totals to the income statement.

Generate the asset templates required in scope (S.06.02 list of assets, S.08.01 derivatives where held) from the investment holdings file and check the CIC codes and counterparty identifiers are populated.
Record a variance note for any line moving more than 10% from the prior reference date, with the business reason.
checklist.done: the balance sheet and performance templates foot to the ledger and every material movement carries a written explanation.

checklist.step: Produce the technical provision and long-term guarantee templates
actions: Generate S.12.01 life technical provisions from the actuarial extract and agree the best estimate and risk margin by line of business to the model run report.
Generate S.22.01 showing the impact of the long-term guarantee measures and transitionals, including the effect of setting the matching adjustment to zero.
Check the technical provision total on S.12.01 agrees to the technical provision line on S.02.01 to the pound.
Attach the model run id and the Model Risk Manager sign-off reference to the template pack.
checklist.done: S.12.01 and S.22.01 agree to the validated model run and to S.02.01 with no residual difference.

checklist.step: Produce own funds, SCR and MCR templates including EPIFP
actions: Generate S.23.01 own funds, classifying each item by tier and applying the eligibility limits, and enter the EPIFP figure supplied by the Valuation Actuary in the prescribed cell.
Generate the SCR templates in scope (S.25 series for the standard formula or the internal model equivalent) and check the risk module aggregation and the diversification benefit recompute.
Generate the S.28 series MCR templates and confirm the MCR sits within the floor and cap corridor around the SCR.
Recompute the SCR and MCR coverage ratios from eligible own funds and record them on the submission cover sheet.
checklist.done: own funds, SCR and MCR templates are produced with EPIFP populated and the coverage ratios recomputed independently of the engine.

checklist.step: Produce the UK National Specific Templates in scope
actions: Generate each National Specific Template still in scope after the PS15/24 reduction, taking the scope list signed at the start of the cycle.
For the matching adjustment templates, agree the asset and liability cash flow columns to the matching adjustment portfolio records held by Investment Operations.
For business model analysis templates, agree the revenue and expense splits to the management accounts and explain any allocation basis used.
Record the source system and owner against every NST on the template inventory.
checklist.done: every in-scope National Specific Template is produced with a named source and an agreed reconciliation.

checklist.step: Build the XBRL instance against the correct taxonomy version
actions: Select the PRA taxonomy version that matches the reference date in the reporting engine and confirm the version string in the instance header.
Generate the XBRL instance document for the full in-scope template set, with the correct entity LEI, reporting currency GBP and reference date.
Run the local validation pack before upload and clear every blocking rule; document each non-blocking rule that will be left with its justification.
Save the instance file with the naming convention <LEI>-<reference date>-<version>.xbrl in the reporting evidence folder.
checklist.done: a validated XBRL instance exists on the correct taxonomy version with all blocking rules cleared and non-blocking rules justified.

checklist.step: Reconcile the instance back to source before attestation
actions: Extract the instance values back out of the XBRL file and place them alongside the ledger extract, the actuarial extract and the holdings file in a reconciliation workbook.
Agree total assets, total technical provisions, total own funds, SCR and MCR from the instance to source, cell by cell.
Investigate any difference above GBP 0.5m to root cause and re-run the instance rather than adjusting the workbook.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the submission pack.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation shows the instance values agree to ledger and actuarial source within GBP 0.5m on every key total.

checklist.step: Obtain internal review and executive attestation
actions: Review the submission pack: template scope list, reconciliation, validation report, coverage ratios and movement commentary.
Challenge the material movements and any non-blocking validation rule left unresolved, and require the Regulatory Reporting Manager to answer in writing.
Sign the attestation that the return is complete and accurate and prepared in accordance with the PRA Rulebook Reporting Part.
Confirm with the Chief Actuary that the technical provision templates rest on an approved actuarial run before signing the annual return.
checklist.done: a dated CFO attestation and Chief Actuary confirmation are on file before the instance is uploaded.

checklist.step: Submit the return through the BEEDS portal
actions: Log in to the Bank of England BEEDS portal with the firm's registered user account and open the return for the correct entity and reference date.
Upload the XBRL instance to the return slot, wait for the portal validation to complete and read the returned validation report in full.
Where BEEDS raises blocking errors, correct at source, rebuild the instance and re-upload — never edit the instance file by hand.
Confirm the return status moves to submitted, download the submission receipt with the reference number and file it in the reporting evidence folder.
checklist.done: BEEDS shows the return as submitted for the correct reference date and the receipt with its reference number is filed.

checklist.step: Prove the submission met the 30 or 70 business day deadline
actions: Compute the deadline as the reference date plus 30 business days for a quarterly return or plus 70 business days for the annual return, using the England and Wales business-day calendar.
Compare the BEEDS receipt timestamp to the computed deadline and record the margin in business days.
Where the margin is under 3 business days, raise a process improvement action naming the step that consumed the float.
Update the reporting calendar entry to closed with the receipt reference attached.
checklist.done: the deadline is computed and the receipt timestamp is shown to fall on or before it, with the margin recorded.

checklist.step: Control any resubmission and notify the PRA
actions: Where an error is found after submission, assess materiality against the SCR coverage ratio and the affected template totals and record the assessment.
Obtain CFO approval for the resubmission and rebuild the instance from corrected source data, never from the submitted file.
Resubmit in BEEDS against the same reference date and email the PRA supervision contact explaining what changed, why, and the control fix.
Log the resubmission in the filing tracker with the affected templates, the cause and the preventive action owner.
checklist.done: every resubmission has a materiality assessment, CFO approval, a PRA explanation and a logged preventive action.

checklist.step: Archive the submission evidence for 10 years
actions: File the XBRL instance, BEEDS receipt, validation report, reconciliation, template scope list and attestation under REG-023/Returns/<reference date>.
Apply the 10-year retention label from the submission date and lock the folder against edits.
Index the record by entity LEI, reference date, BEEDS reference number and taxonomy version.
Confirm the previous four reference dates are still retrievable in one search.
checklist.done: the submission pack is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable by BEEDS reference number and reference date.

testing.step: Build the population of returns and templates for the year
actions: Extract from BEEDS the list of returns submitted for the entity across the four quarterly reference dates and the annual reference date, with submission timestamps and reference numbers.
Explode each return into its submitted templates by parsing the XBRL instance table list, producing one population row per template per reference date.
Add a row for every resubmission recorded in the filing tracker.
Reconcile the population template count to the signed template scope list for each reference date and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the signed scope lists for all five reference dates and includes every resubmission.

testing.step: Reconcile the submitted scope to the PRA taxonomy requirement
actions: Download the PRA taxonomy template list for each reference date independently of the preparer.
Compare it to the templates actually present in each submitted instance and list templates required but absent and templates submitted but not required.
Test each claimed non-applicability against the entity's business: matching adjustment use, internal model status, line of business written.
Record any required template omitted as an automatic exception, not a scoping judgement.
testing.done: every required template is present in the submitted instance or the omission is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the template sample
actions: Take 100% of S.02.01, S.12.01, S.23.01, the S.25 series and the S.28 series across all five reference dates because they drive the solvency position.
Take 20 further templates at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, weighted to National Specific Templates.
Take 100% of resubmissions.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and scope list version in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all solvency-driving templates and all resubmissions is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the template-to-source reconciliation
actions: For each sampled balance sheet template, pull the trial balance for the reference date directly from the general ledger rather than using the preparer's extract.
Apply the Solvency UK valuation adjustments journal and independently derive the total asset and other liability figures.
Compare to the submitted S.02.01 values and record the difference for each line.
Treat any difference above GBP 0.5m without a documented, approved mapping change as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled balance sheet template re-derives from the general ledger within GBP 0.5m or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the own funds, SCR, MCR and EPIFP calculations
actions: Recompute eligible own funds by tier from the S.23.01 basic own funds items, applying the tier eligibility limits independently.
Recompute the SCR aggregation across risk modules from the S.25 series inputs and check the diversification benefit and the loss-absorbing capacity adjustments.
Recompute the MCR from its linear inputs and confirm it sits inside the corridor around the SCR.
Recompute the EPIFP figure using the prescribed method from the model cash flows and compare to the submitted cell, treating any difference as an exception to the Chief Actuary.
testing.done: own funds by tier, SCR, MCR and EPIFP all recompute to the submitted values or the differences are quantified and escalated.

testing.step: Re-run validation on the submitted instance in the regulator's own tooling
actions: Retrieve the submitted XBRL instance from the evidence archive and confirm its hash matches the file uploaded to BEEDS.
Open the BEEDS validation report for that submission and list every rule that fired, separating blocking from non-blocking.
Confirm no blocking rule was open at the point the return reached submitted status.
For every non-blocking rule left unresolved, read the recorded justification and judge whether it explains the data or merely restates the rule.
testing.done: the archived instance matches the submitted file, no blocking rule was open at submission, and each non-blocking rule has a substantive justification.

testing.step: Trace attestation and approval to the submission event
actions: For each sampled reference date, obtain the CFO attestation and the Chief Actuary confirmation and read their dates and versions.
Confirm the attestation pre-dates the BEEDS submission timestamp and refers to the same instance version that was uploaded.
Confirm the BEEDS submitting user is on the authorised submitter list and is not the same person who prepared the sampled templates.
Log any submission made without a pre-dated attestation or by an unauthorised user as a control failure.
testing.done: every sampled submission has a pre-dated attestation for the uploaded version and was made by an authorised, segregated submitter.

testing.step: Recompute the 30 and 70 business day deadlines
actions: Recompute each quarterly deadline as the reference date plus 30 business days and the annual deadline as 31 December plus 70 business days, listing the England and Wales bank holidays applied.
Compare each recomputed deadline to the BEEDS receipt timestamp and record the margin in business days.
Confirm any resubmission after the deadline was notified to the PRA supervision contact and the notification date is on file.
Any submission after the recomputed deadline is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: all five deadlines are recomputed with a stated holiday calendar and each submission is proven timely or a breach is reported.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception naming the reference date, the template, the value tested and the difference found.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: scope list stale, mapping break overridden, model run not approved, taxonomy version wrong, attestation late, calendar wrong.
Name an owner and a remediation date, and require the fix to be evidenced at the next reference date rather than by assertion.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue id, root cause, owner, remediation date and a next-cycle retest row.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sampled templates and compare it to the zero-late-submission and zero-open-blocking-rule thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the reconciliation and recomputation workpapers.
Have the reviewer — who prepared and attested none of the sampled templates — sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any late submission and any resubmission count above two to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an exception rate, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date is filed.

In-scope systems.value: Annual supplemental schedules are generated in the regulatory reporting engine from the general ledger, the reinsurance administration system and the matching adjustment portfolio records

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Supplemental Schedule Procedure FIN-SUK-05 — schedule inventory with source system and preparer, matching adjustment asset-liability cash flow build, intra-group transaction capture rules, variation analysis walk method, and the review evidence required per schedule

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and the Chief Actuary jointly because the matching adjustment exhibits depend on actuarial cash flows; refreshed annually when the PRA publishes the reference-date template list

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual-only schedules must be complete and reconciled 15 business days before the 70-business-day annual return deadline so they can be included in the single annual BEEDS instance; the matching adjustment exhibits carry an internal cut-off 25 business days before submission

Deadline reminders configured.value: Schedule inventory tasks alert at 31 December +30, +45 and +55 business days per schedule owner, with escalation to the Controller if any schedule has no reconciliation attached by +55

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A schedule omitted from the annual instance, an unreconciled schedule, or a restated matching adjustment exhibit is logged with the schedule code, cause and remediation owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Controller signs off every schedule restatement; the Chief Actuary co-signs where a matching adjustment or technical provision exhibit is restated

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every annual-only schedule and National Specific Template in the reference-date scope list, together with every underlying reinsurance treaty, intra-group transaction and matching adjustment asset holding feeding them

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero in-scope schedules missing from the annual instance; every schedule must reconcile to its named source within GBP 0.5m; the matching adjustment asset cash flows must reproduce the disclosed portfolio value within 0.5%; any schedule without a named reviewer sign-off is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once per year in the 10 business days before the annual submission, covering the full schedule inventory rather than a sample of it

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must have prepared no schedule and must not report into the Controller's statutory reporting team

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual supplemental schedule testing workpaper (inventory completeness check, per-schedule reconciliation re-performance, matching adjustment cash flow recomputation, exception log) filed under REG-023/Annual-Schedules/<year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Schedule inventory with source mapping, per-schedule reconciliations, the matching adjustment asset and liability cash flow file, and the treaty and intra-group source listings, producible to the PRA within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Controller answers PRA questions on the supplemental schedules with the Chief Actuary on matching adjustment exhibits; Regulatory Counsel clears any correction of a submitted schedule before it is filed

checklist.step: Build the annual schedule inventory from the reference-date template list
actions: Take the PRA annual template list for the reference date and strip out the templates already produced in the quarterly return to leave the annual-only set.
Add every National Specific Template retained after the PS15/24 reduction that applies to a solo life and annuity firm using the matching adjustment.
For each schedule record the code, the source system, the named preparer, the named reviewer and the internal due date.
Circulate the inventory to the Controller and the Chief Actuary for joint approval before preparation starts.
checklist.done: an approved inventory lists every annual-only schedule with a code, source system, preparer, reviewer and due date.

checklist.step: Produce the variation analysis schedules explaining the movement in own funds
actions: Pull the opening and closing excess of assets over liabilities from the frozen Solvency UK balance sheets for the prior and current reference dates.
Build the analysis of change walk: new business, expected return and unwind, assumption changes, experience variances, model changes, capital movements and dividends.
Populate the S.29 series variation analysis templates and confirm the walk closes to the actual movement with a residual of nil.
Write a one-line business explanation for every step over GBP 5m and get the Head of Capital Management to confirm it.
checklist.done: the variation analysis closes to the actual own funds movement with no residual and every material step is explained.

checklist.step: Produce the reinsurance schedules from the treaty records
actions: Extract every treaty and facultative arrangement in force at 31 December from the reinsurance administration system with reinsurer name, LEI, credit rating, share and coverage period.
Populate the S.30 and S.31 series reinsurance templates with the ceded shares, the reinsurer identifiers and the recoverable amounts.
Agree the total reinsurance recoverable to the recoverables line on S.02.01 and to the ceded balance in the general ledger.
Confirm every reinsurer identifier and rating with the Reinsurance Credit and Security Analyst and file the confirmation.
checklist.done: the reinsurance schedules list every in-force arrangement and the recoverable total agrees to S.02.01 and the ledger.

checklist.step: Capture intra-group transactions and risk concentrations
actions: Run the intercompany account analysis for the year and list every transaction with a group entity: capital injections, loans, guarantees, internal reinsurance, cost recharges and dividends.
Populate the intra-group transaction templates with counterparty name, LEI, transaction type, value and date, and flag transactions above the internal materiality threshold.
Build the risk concentration template from the largest counterparty exposures across investments, reinsurance and cash, taking the exposure file from Investment Operations.
Reconcile the intercompany totals to the group reporting pack and clear any difference with the group Controller.
checklist.done: every intra-group transaction and top counterparty exposure is captured and reconciles to the group reporting pack.

checklist.step: Build the matching adjustment asset and liability cash flow exhibit
actions: Extract the matching adjustment portfolio asset list at the reference date with ISIN, CIC code, nominal, market value, contractual cash flows and credit rating.
Extract the matched annuity liability cash flows from the approved valuation run for the same portfolio and reference date.
Populate the matching adjustment National Specific Templates with the asset and liability cash flows by projection year and the resulting fundamental spread deductions.
Test the cash flow matching quality against the matching adjustment eligibility tests and record the tested values, not just a pass flag.
checklist.done: the matching adjustment exhibit shows asset and liability cash flows by year with the matching tests re-performed and their values recorded.

checklist.step: Produce the business model analysis templates
actions: Take the management accounts and split premiums, claims, expenses and investment return by product group in line with the National Specific Template layout.
Document the allocation basis used for shared expenses and confirm it with the FP&A Manager in writing.
Populate the revenue account templates and agree the totals to S.05.01 and to the income statement.
Record a variance note for any product group whose result moved more than 15% year on year.
checklist.done: the business model analysis templates foot to S.05.01 and the income statement with a documented, confirmed allocation basis.

checklist.step: Produce the asset detail and look-through schedules
actions: Extract the full holdings file at the reference date with ISIN, CIC code, issuer, issuer group, country, currency, rating, duration and market value.
Apply look-through to collective investment holdings so exposures are reported at underlying asset level where required.
Populate the annual asset detail templates and agree the total market value to the investment line on S.02.01.
List any holding with a missing CIC code, rating or issuer LEI and clear it with the custodian before release.
checklist.done: the asset schedules carry complete identifiers, apply look-through, and total to the S.02.01 investment line.

checklist.step: Reconcile every schedule to its named source
actions: For each schedule on the inventory, build a one-page reconciliation showing the schedule total, the source system total and the difference.
Cross-check the schedule totals that must agree to the primary templates: reinsurance recoverables to S.02.01, technical provisions to S.12.01, revenue to S.05.01, own funds movement to S.23.01.
Investigate every difference above GBP 0.5m to root cause and correct at source rather than on the schedule.
Attach the signed reconciliation to the schedule in the reporting evidence folder.
checklist.done: each schedule carries a signed one-page reconciliation to its source with no unexplained difference above GBP 0.5m.

checklist.step: Run the second-person review over each schedule
actions: Assign each schedule to the reviewer named on the inventory, who must not be the preparer.
The reviewer checks the source extract date, the reconciliation, the identifiers and codes, and the prior-year comparative movement.
The reviewer records specific review notes — which cells were vouched and to what — rather than a blanket approval.
Hold any schedule with open review notes out of the instance until they are cleared.
checklist.done: every schedule carries dated reviewer notes naming the cells vouched, and no schedule with open notes enters the instance.

checklist.step: Apply cross-template validation before inclusion in the instance
actions: Load the schedules into the reporting engine for the annual reference date and run the cross-template validation rule set.
Focus on the rules that link annual schedules to the core templates: reinsurance to S.02.01, variation analysis to S.23.01, asset detail to S.06.02.
Clear every blocking rule at source and document each non-blocking rule left open with a substantive data explanation.
Archive the validation report alongside the schedule pack.
checklist.done: cross-template validation runs clean of blocking rules and each open non-blocking rule has a data explanation on file.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Actuary sign-off on the actuarially derived schedules
actions: Review the matching adjustment exhibits, the technical provision detail schedules and the variation analysis assumption-change steps.
Confirm each rests on an approved model run with a recorded run id and a Model Risk Manager validation reference.
Challenge any assumption-change step in the variation analysis that is not traceable to a documented assumption-setting decision.
Sign the actuarial schedules and record the signature date on the schedule inventory.
checklist.done: every actuarially derived schedule carries a dated Chief Actuary signature and an approved model run reference.

checklist.step: Include the schedules in the annual BEEDS instance and confirm acceptance
actions: Regenerate the annual XBRL instance so it contains the core templates plus every schedule on the approved inventory.
Check the instance table list against the inventory line by line and confirm no schedule is missing.
Upload to the BEEDS portal, read the validation report and confirm the return status reaches submitted.
Download the submission receipt and mark each schedule on the inventory as submitted with the receipt reference.
checklist.done: the annual instance contains every inventory schedule and the BEEDS receipt reference is recorded against each one.

checklist.step: Prepare the supporting file the PRA will ask for
actions: Assemble a single supporting file per schedule: source extract, reconciliation, reviewer notes, sign-offs and the validation report.
Add a one-page methodology note for the judgemental schedules — expense allocation basis, look-through approach, matching adjustment cash flow construction.
Index the file so any schedule code can be produced within one working day of a PRA request.
Have the Controller confirm the pack is complete before the reporting cycle is closed.
checklist.done: a per-schedule supporting file with a methodology note exists and the Controller has confirmed completeness.

checklist.step: Log and remediate any schedule defect found after submission
actions: Assess any post-submission defect for effect on own funds, SCR coverage or the matching adjustment benefit and record the assessment.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether the defect requires a resubmission or a note at the next reference date, and record the reasoning.
Raise a tracker issue with the schedule code, cause, owner and the control change that prevents recurrence.
Where the matching adjustment exhibits are affected, notify the Chief Actuary the same day.
checklist.done: every post-submission defect has a quantified impact assessment, a resubmit-or-note decision and a preventive control change.

checklist.step: Archive the annual schedule pack under the retention rule
actions: File the schedule inventory, each schedule with its supporting file, the Chief Actuary sign-offs and the BEEDS receipt under REG-023/Annual-Schedules/<year>.
Apply the 10-year retention label from the annual submission date and lock the folder.
Index by schedule code, reference date and BEEDS reference number.
Confirm the matching adjustment cash flow file is retained in its native format, not only as a PDF print.
checklist.done: the annual schedule pack is archived for 10 years, indexed by schedule code, with cash flow files in native format.

testing.step: Build the population of annual schedules and their sources
actions: Parse the submitted annual XBRL instance and list every table it contains, separating the annual-only schedules from the core templates.
Add every in-force reinsurance treaty, every intra-group transaction and every matching adjustment holding from the underlying source systems as detail-level population rows.
Reconcile the schedule list to the approved schedule inventory and the PRA reference-date template list.
Sign the population as complete and record the template list version used.
testing.done: the population covers every submitted schedule plus its detail records and reconciles to both the inventory and the PRA template list.

testing.step: Test inventory completeness against the PRA requirement independently
actions: Download the PRA annual template list for the reference date without reference to the preparer's inventory.
Mark each template as required or not required for a solo life and annuity firm using the matching adjustment, recording the basis for each not-required call.
Compare the resulting required list to the tables actually present in the submitted instance.
Log every required schedule absent from the instance as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the independently derived required list matches the submitted schedule set or every gap is logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the schedule and detail sample
actions: Take 100% of the schedules at schedule level because the inventory is small.
At detail level take 25 reinsurance arrangements, 25 matching adjustment holdings and all intra-group transactions above the materiality threshold, selected with a recorded seed.
Record the seed, the detail population sizes and the selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn.
Include every schedule restated after first preparation.
testing.done: all schedules and a reproducible detail sample of treaties, holdings and intra-group items are documented with the seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the reinsurance schedule from the treaty records
actions: For each sampled arrangement, open the treaty record and read the reinsurer, LEI, share, coverage period and any limits directly from the contract slip.
Recompute the ceded share and the recoverable at the reference date and compare to the value reported on the S.30 or S.31 schedule.
Confirm the reinsurer credit rating on the schedule matches the rating held by the Reinsurance Credit and Security Analyst at the reference date.
Flag any arrangement in force at year end that does not appear on the schedule as a completeness exception.
testing.done: each sampled arrangement re-performs to the reported recoverable and no in-force arrangement is missing from the schedule.

testing.step: Recompute the matching adjustment asset and liability cash flows
actions: Pull the matching adjustment portfolio holdings independently at the reference date and rebuild the contractual asset cash flows by projection year from instrument terms.
Compare the rebuilt asset cash flow profile to the profile reported on the matching adjustment schedule year by year.
Re-perform the cash flow matching tests against the eligibility criteria and record the computed test statistics rather than a pass flag.
Treat a reported portfolio value differing from the rebuilt value by more than 0.5% as an exception to the Chief Actuary.
testing.done: the matching adjustment cash flow profile rebuilds within 0.5% and the matching tests re-perform with recorded statistics.

testing.step: Re-perform the variation analysis walk on own funds
actions: Take the prior and current reference-date excess of assets over liabilities from the audited balance sheets, not the preparer's schedule.
Sum the reported walk steps on the S.29 series and confirm they close to the actual movement with a nil residual.
For the three largest steps, trace to the underlying evidence: the new business report, the assumption change paper, or the capital transaction approval.
Log any step above GBP 5m without traceable evidence as an exception.
testing.done: the variation analysis walk closes to the audited movement and the three largest steps trace to primary evidence.

testing.step: Trace intra-group transactions to their approvals and the ledger
actions: For each sampled intra-group transaction, open the intercompany account in the general ledger and agree counterparty, amount, date and transaction type.
Trace each capital injection, loan, guarantee and dividend to the board or committee approval that authorised it.
Run the intercompany account analysis independently for the year and check no material transaction is absent from the schedule.
Log unapproved or unreported intra-group transactions as exceptions to the Chief Financial Officer.
testing.done: every sampled intra-group item agrees to the ledger and to an approval, and the independent run finds no omissions.

testing.step: Test preparer and reviewer segregation and sign-off dating
actions: For each schedule, read the preparer and reviewer names from the inventory and confirm they are different individuals.
Confirm the reviewer notes name specific cells vouched rather than recording a blanket approval.
Confirm the Chief Actuary signature on the actuarially derived schedules pre-dates the BEEDS submission timestamp.
Log self-reviewed schedules and post-submission sign-offs as control failures.
testing.done: every schedule shows distinct preparer and reviewer, specific review notes, and sign-offs dated before submission.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception naming the schedule code, the detail record and the difference quantified.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: inventory incomplete, source extract stale, look-through not applied, identifiers missing, allocation basis undocumented, self-review.
Name an owner and a remediation date and require the fix to be evidenced in next year's schedule pack.
Escalate matching adjustment exceptions to the Chief Actuary within one business day given their effect on technical provisions.
testing.done: every exception has an issue id, quantified difference, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate at schedule and detail level and compare to the zero-missing-schedule and GBP 0.5m reconciliation thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the re-performance workpapers.
Have the reviewer — who prepared and reviewed no schedule and does not report to the Controller — sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any matching adjustment exception to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with schedule-level and detail-level exception rates and a stated conclusion is filed.
