checklist.step: Hold the audit planning meeting and agree the scope and timetable
actions: Convene the planning meeting with the engagement partner, the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee Chair before the year end.
Agree the audit scope: statutory accounts, and the relevant elements of the SFCR being the Valuation for Solvency Purposes and Capital Management sections and the associated templates.
Agree materiality, the reporting threshold for unadjusted differences, and the significant risk areas — annuity technical provisions, matching adjustment eligibility and illiquid asset valuation.
Publish the timetable with the interim controls visit, the PBC delivery date, the clearance meeting and the signing date, and load the milestones into the audit platform.
checklist.done: a signed audit plan states scope, materiality, significant risks and dated milestones through to report signing.

checklist.step: Confirm auditor independence and clear non-audit services
actions: Obtain the audit firm's written independence confirmation for the engagement, covering the firm, the engagement partner and the network.
List every non-audit service the firm provided in the year with the fee, the service description and the pre-approval reference.
Test each service against the Audit Committee's permitted-services policy and the fee ratio cap, and escalate any service without pre-approval.
Table the independence confirmation and the fee analysis at the Audit Committee and minute the conclusion.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has minuted an independence conclusion supported by a fee analysis with a pre-approval reference for every non-audit service.

checklist.step: Own and deliver the prepared-by-client list
actions: Load the PBC list into the audit platform with an owner and a due date against every item.
Deliver each item as a dated, version-controlled file with the source system and extract date stated on it.
Chase owners at 5 and 2 business days before due date and escalate any item still open on the due date to the Controller.
Track the delivery rate weekly and report it at the audit progress call.
checklist.done: every PBC item is delivered with a stated source and extract date, and the open-item list is nil at the clearance meeting.

checklist.step: Support the audit of technical provisions and the matching adjustment
actions: Give the auditor's actuarial specialists the model run id, the assumption-setting papers and the Model Risk Manager validation report for the year-end run.
Walk them through the best estimate and risk margin build, the cost-of-capital rate applied and the matching adjustment eligibility testing.
Answer specialist queries in writing within 3 business days and log each query and answer in the audit platform.
Escalate to the Chief Financial Officer any auditor challenge that would move technical provisions by more than materiality.
checklist.done: the actuarial specialists have the run references and assumption papers, and every query has a logged written answer.

checklist.step: Support the audit of the SFCR relevant elements
actions: Provide the Section D and Section E drafts, the tie-out schedule and the QRT annex to the audit team at the agreed milestone.
Reconcile own funds by tier, SCR and MCR from source to the disclosed figures in a schedule the auditor can foot independently.
Explain and evidence the tier classification of each own funds item and the eligibility limits applied.
Record every audit query on the relevant elements and its resolution against the tie-out schedule line.
checklist.done: the auditor holds a footable reconciliation of own funds, SCR and MCR and every relevant-element query is resolved on the tie-out schedule.

checklist.step: Route and decide audit adjustments and unadjusted differences
actions: Log each proposed audit adjustment with the amount, the affected account and the auditor's rationale.
Post accepted adjustments in the close tool as a separate audit adjustment journal so they can be identified after the fact.
Record each rejected adjustment on the summary of unadjusted differences with the reason and the effect on profit, equity and own funds.
Confirm the aggregate unadjusted difference stays below materiality and present it to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: accepted adjustments are posted in an identifiable journal and every unadjusted difference is quantified on a schedule below materiality.

checklist.step: Assess the four key functions for independence and resource
actions: For risk management, compliance, internal audit and the actuarial function, document the reporting line, the SMF holder, the direct access to the board and the escalation route.
Confirm no function head has operational responsibility for a business area they review, and record where a shared resource creates a conflict and how it is managed.
Record headcount, budget, key skills and turnover for each function and compare to the plan agreed at the start of the year.
Present the assessment to the board Risk Committee with a stated conclusion on operational independence and adequacy of resource under Conditions Governing Business 4 to 6.
checklist.done: each key function has a documented reporting line, conflict analysis and resource comparison with a board-level independence conclusion.

checklist.step: Confirm the internal audit function's coverage and unrestricted access
actions: Compare the year's completed audit plan to the approved plan and explain every deferred or cancelled engagement.
Confirm internal audit had unrestricted access to records, systems and staff, and log any instance where access was refused or delayed.
Confirm the internal audit charter, board approval date and the reporting line to the Audit Committee Chair remain current.
Report plan completion, access issues and open findings to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: plan completion is reported with reasons for deferrals and a written statement on unrestricted access.

checklist.step: Confirm the actuarial function report is produced and reaches the board
actions: Produce the annual actuarial function report covering technical provisions reliability, underwriting policy opinion and reinsurance adequacy opinion.
State any material reservation on data quality or assumption setting explicitly rather than in a general caveat.
Table the report at the board and minute the board's consideration of it.
File the report and the minute reference with the key function assessment.
checklist.done: the actuarial function report with explicit opinions is tabled at the board and the consideration is minuted.

checklist.step: Sign the management representation letter
actions: Read the draft representation letter and challenge any representation the firm cannot evidence.
Obtain supporting confirmations from the Chief Actuary on technical provisions, the General Counsel on litigation and the Chief Risk Officer on regulatory correspondence.
Date the letter on the same day the audit reports are signed, not before.
File the signed letter with the audit reports in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: a signed representation letter dated the same day as the audit reports is on file with its supporting confirmations.

checklist.step: Take the audit findings report and the accounts to the Audit Committee
actions: Load the audit findings report, the draft accounts, the unadjusted differences schedule and the independence confirmation into the board portal 5 business days before the meeting.
Give the Audit Committee a private session with the engagement partner with no executives present, and minute that it took place.
Minute the committee's recommendation to the board to approve the accounts and any conditions attached.
Circulate the minute to the Controller as the authority to have the reports signed.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has met the auditor privately and minuted a recommendation to approve, with the papers issued 5 business days in advance.

checklist.step: Obtain the signed audit reports on the accounts and the SFCR relevant elements
actions: Confirm the board has approved the accounts and collect the signed auditor's report on the statutory financial statements.
Collect the separate auditor's report on the relevant elements of the SFCR and check it names the sections and templates it covers.
Read both reports for modifications, emphasis of matter and material uncertainty paragraphs, and brief the Chief Financial Officer on anything other than a clean opinion.
File both signed reports in the financial reporting repository against the reporting year.
checklist.done: both signed reports are on file, their scope is checked, and any modification has been briefed to the CFO.

checklist.step: Notify the PRA where the opinion or findings warrant it
actions: Assess whether a modified opinion, a material uncertainty paragraph or a significant control deficiency is something the PRA would reasonably expect notice of.
Where it is, draft the notification with Regulatory Counsel setting out the finding, the impact on own funds or SCR coverage and the remediation plan with dates.
Send it to the named PRA supervision contact and record the date sent and any acknowledgement.
Report the notification to the board Risk Committee at its next meeting.
checklist.done: any modified opinion or significant deficiency is assessed and, where notifiable, sent to the PRA with a dated record.

checklist.step: File the audited accounts and track finding remediation to closure
actions: Confirm the audited financial statements are filed within the statutory Companies House filing period and record the filing confirmation.
Load every audit finding and control deficiency into the audit platform with a management response, an owner and a remediation date.
Verify closure with evidence — a re-performed control, a reconciliation, a system change record — not with an owner assertion.
Report open findings past their remediation date to the Audit Committee at every meeting until closed.
checklist.done: the accounts are filed within the statutory period and every finding is tracked with evidence-based closure verification.

checklist.step: Archive the audit evidence pack
actions: File the audit plan, PBC delivery log, findings report, management responses, representation letter, both signed audit reports, independence confirmations and the key function assessment under REG-023/Audit/<year>.
Apply the 10-year retention label from the audit report date and lock the folder against edits.
Index by reporting year, audit firm, engagement partner and opinion type.
Confirm the prior three years remain retrievable in a single search.
checklist.done: the audit evidence pack is archived for 10 years and retrievable by reporting year and opinion type.

testing.step: Build the population of audit outputs and key function assertions
actions: Extract from the audit platform every finding, control deficiency and unadjusted difference raised in the audit cycle, with owner, response and remediation date.
Add every non-audit service engagement with the audit firm in the year from the accounts payable ledger, not only from the firm's own list.
Add one row per key function (risk management, compliance, internal audit, actuarial) for the independence and resource assertions.
Reconcile the finding count to the audit findings report tabled at the Audit Committee and resolve any difference.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the tabled findings report and includes ledger-sourced non-audit services and all four key functions.

testing.step: Reconcile the audited figures to the published accounts and the SFCR
actions: Take the signed audit report and identify the exact financial statements and SFCR sections and templates within its scope.
Agree total assets, total liabilities, profit and equity from the signed accounts to the final close tool version.
Agree own funds, SCR and MCR in the SFCR Capital Management section to the templates named in the SFCR relevant-elements audit report.
Log any figure published outside the audit scope that a reader would assume was audited.
testing.done: the audited scope is mapped to the published figures and any unaudited figure presented alongside audited ones is identified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of findings and services
actions: Take 100% of significant findings, all unadjusted differences above the reporting threshold and all four key function rows.
Take 15 further findings at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population.
Take 100% of non-audit service engagements above the de minimis fee threshold.
Record the seed, the population sizes and the selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all significant findings, key functions and material non-audit services is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the auditor independence assessment
actions: Total the non-audit fees paid to the audit firm and its network from the accounts payable ledger and compute the ratio to the audit fee.
Compare each sampled service to the Audit Committee's permitted-services policy and locate its pre-approval reference in the committee minutes.
Check for prohibited services — bookkeeping, valuation feeding the accounts, internal audit outsourcing — regardless of pre-approval.
Log any service without pre-approval, any prohibited service and any breach of the fee ratio as an independence exception to the Audit Committee Chair.
testing.done: the fee ratio recomputes from the ledger and every sampled service is matched to a minuted pre-approval or logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the key function independence test against the organisation chart
actions: Pull the reporting lines for each key function head and their direct reports from the HRIS as at the reference date, independently of the assessment paper.
Confirm no key function head reports to, or is remunerated by, a business area within their review scope.
Confirm each function head holds direct access to the board or the relevant committee by locating a minute where they reported without an executive intermediary.
Compare actual headcount and vacancy duration to the resource plan and quantify any gap in full-time equivalents.
testing.done: reporting lines are verified from the HRIS, direct board access is evidenced by a minute, and resource gaps are quantified in FTE.

testing.step: Trace the management representation letter and its supporting confirmations
actions: Read each representation in the signed letter and identify the internal confirmation that supports it.
Confirm the Chief Actuary, General Counsel and Chief Risk Officer confirmations exist, are dated on or before the letter date and cover the representations attributed to them.
Confirm the letter date matches the audit report signing date.
Log any representation with no supporting confirmation as an exception.
testing.done: every representation traces to a dated internal confirmation and the letter date matches the report signing date.

testing.step: Test remediation closure evidence on sampled findings
actions: For each sampled finding marked closed, open the closure evidence and judge whether it demonstrates the control now operates — a re-performance, a reconciliation, a change record.
Reject closures supported only by an owner statement or a plan document and reopen them in the platform.
For findings still open, compare the current date to the agreed remediation date and compute the days overdue.
Check overdue findings were reported to the Audit Committee at every meeting since they went overdue.
testing.done: each closed finding has operational closure evidence and every overdue finding has an evidenced committee reporting trail.

testing.step: Recompute the audit and filing deadline compliance
actions: Compare the SFCR relevant-elements report date to the SFCR board approval date and confirm the 10-business-day lead was met.
Confirm the accounts audit report date precedes the board approval of the accounts and the Companies House filing date.
Recompute the Companies House filing deadline from the accounting reference date and compare to the filing confirmation timestamp.
Any report signed after the approval it supports, or a filing after the statutory period, is a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every report and filing date is recomputed against its deadline and the sequence of signing and approval is proven correct.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the finding, service or key function and what failed.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: pre-approval bypassed, closure evidence insufficient, reporting line conflict, resource gap unfilled, representation unsupported, timetable slipped.
Name an owner and a remediation date, and route independence exceptions to the Audit Committee Chair the same day.
Carry every open exception into next year's audit assurance test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue id, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare to the zero-unapproved-non-audit-service and zero-conflicted-key-function thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective on both the audit coordination control and the Conditions Governing Business 4 to 6 key function requirement.
Have the reviewer — who sits outside finance and prepared no audited balance — sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee and the board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with separate conclusions on audit coordination and key function independence is filed and reported.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Solvency UK regulatory calendar for the UK entity — every PRA return, notification and disclosure date and the evidence that each was met on time

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — deadlines re-derived each year from the PRA Rulebook Reporting Part with PS15/24 (quarterly 30 business days, annual 70 business days after the reference date), the SFCR publication rule in Reporting 3 with PS3/24, and the ORSA supervisory report timing in Conditions Governing Business

In-scope processes.value: Continuous calendar maintenance for the UK solo entity: quarterly and annual QRT/NST returns, the SFCR, the ORSA supervisory report, ad hoc PRA data requests and notification obligations, with a timeliness evidence record per event

In-scope systems.value: The obligations register holds one calendar entry per filing with owner, deadline rule and evidence link; submission receipts come from BEEDS and the website publication log

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulatory Calendar Procedure REG-SUK-02 — how each deadline is derived from its rule rather than copied forward, the business-day calendar used, the owner and deputy per entry, the horizon-scanning intake for new obligations, and the evidence required to close an entry

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance, refreshed every January when the new-year deadline recalculation runs, and re-approved on any PRA policy statement that changes a reporting deadline

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: All of them, and each entry stores the derivation not just the date: quarterly returns at reference date plus 30 business days, the annual return and the SFCR at 31 December plus 70 business days, the ORSA supervisory report within two weeks of board conclusion, and ad hoc PRA requests at the date stated in the request

Deadline reminders configured.value: Every entry fires alerts at T-30, T-15, T-5 and T-1 business days to the owner and deputy, and an amber-to-red status change at T-5 if no draft evidence is attached; overdue entries page the Head of Compliance daily

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Per calendar entry: the deadline derivation, the submission receipt or publication URL with timestamp, the approver, and the closure note — retained 10 years from the entry date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any entry closed after its deadline, closed without evidence, or discovered missing from the calendar is raised as a breach with a PRA notification decision and a calendar control fix

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every late or missing filing breach, the PRA notification decision and the calendar control change that prevents recurrence

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every calendar entry with a due date inside the test period, plus every submission actually made to the PRA in the period, so filings made without a calendar entry are exposed

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero entries closed after their deadline; zero entries closed without a receipt or publication timestamp; zero PRA submissions found with no corresponding calendar entry; any deadline whose stored derivation does not match the current rule is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous, so the test runs quarterly over that quarter's due entries, with an annual pass in January that re-derives every deadline for the new year from the Rulebook

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own or deputise on any calendar entry and must not be able to edit the obligations register

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly regulatory calendar timeliness workpaper (entry population, two-way reconciliation to BEEDS, deadline re-derivation, exception log) filed under REG-023/Calendar/<quarter>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A calendar extract for the period showing each obligation, its rule-based deadline, the actual submission date, the margin in business days and the evidence link — producible to the PRA within 2 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Head of Compliance answers PRA questions on reporting timeliness; a late filing is self-reported to the PRA supervision contact by the Chief Risk Officer with the cause and the control fix rather than waiting to be asked

checklist.step: Re-derive every deadline for the new year from the source rule
actions: Open each Solvency UK obligation in the obligations register and read the stored derivation rule rather than last year's date.
Recompute the quarterly return dates as 31 March, 30 June and 30 September plus 30 business days, and the annual return and SFCR dates as 31 December plus 70 business days.
Apply the published England and Wales bank holiday list for the new year and record which holidays affected each date.
Never roll a date forward by 365 days — replace it with the recomputed date and log the change with the recalculation date.
checklist.done: every entry holds a newly computed date with its derivation and the holiday list applied, with no dates carried forward.

checklist.step: Assign an owner and a deputy to every calendar entry
actions: Assign a named owner and a named deputy to each entry, with the deputy in a different team so leave cannot orphan a filing.
Email each owner their entries with the deadline, the derivation and the evidence required to close, and record their acceptance in the register.
Reassign entries owned by leavers within 5 business days of the leaver notification from HR.
Review the ownership grid at the monthly compliance meeting and minute any reassignment.
checklist.done: no entry is unowned, every entry has a deputy from a different team, and leaver reassignment is within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Configure the reminder ladder and the escalation rules
actions: Set alerts on every entry at T-30, T-15, T-5 and T-1 business days to the owner and deputy.
Configure the entry to move to amber at T-15 if no draft evidence is attached and to red at T-5, notifying the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Configure a daily page to the Head of Compliance for any entry that passes its deadline unclosed.
Send a test alert on a dummy entry and confirm delivery to the owner, deputy and escalation mailbox before relying on the ladder.
checklist.done: the reminder ladder and escalations are configured and proven by a delivered test alert.

checklist.step: Run horizon scanning so new obligations reach the calendar
actions: Monitor the PRA publications page, policy statements, consultation papers and Dear CEO letters weekly, plus Bank of England reporting taxonomy announcements.
For each item that creates, removes or moves a deadline, raise a calendar change request naming the obligation, the new rule and the first affected reference date.
Assess the change with the Regulatory Reporting Manager within 10 business days and either create, amend or retire the entry.
Record the source document reference on the entry so the derivation is auditable.
checklist.done: every relevant PRA publication is assessed within 10 business days and results in a dated calendar change or a recorded no-change decision.

checklist.step: Maintain the two-way link between calendar entries and submissions
actions: After each BEEDS submission, attach the receipt with its reference number and timestamp to the matching calendar entry.
Monthly, list every submission made in BEEDS and check each has a calendar entry; create an entry for any submission that has none and investigate why it was missing.
List every entry closed in the month and check each has a receipt or publication URL attached.
Report both gap lists to the Regulatory Reporting Manager with a cause for each gap.
checklist.done: every submission maps to an entry and every closed entry holds a receipt, with both gap lists reported monthly.

checklist.step: Record the timeliness margin at the point of closure
actions: On closing an entry, compute the margin in business days between the receipt timestamp and the stored deadline and write it on the entry.
Attach the approver name and the version of the submitted artefact to the closure note.
Flag any entry closed with a margin under 3 business days for a process review, naming the step that consumed the float.
Refuse to close an entry with no evidence attached, regardless of assurance that the filing was made.
checklist.done: every closed entry shows a computed margin, an approver, an artefact version and attached evidence.

checklist.step: Track the SFCR publication as a calendar obligation in its own right
actions: Hold a separate entry for SFCR publication with the 70-business-day derivation and the board approval date as a predecessor milestone.
Attach the public URL and the web server publication timestamp as the closure evidence, not the internal sign-off.
Add a follow-on entry for the PRA notification of publication with its own owner and date.
Verify the URL resolves from outside the corporate network before closing the entry.
checklist.done: the SFCR entry closes on an externally verified URL and timestamp with the PRA notification tracked as a linked entry.

checklist.step: Track the ORSA supervisory report submission
actions: Create the ORSA entry with its deadline derived as within two weeks of the board concluding the ORSA process, and store the derivation.
Set the board conclusion date on the entry as soon as the board minute is signed, which starts the clock.
Attach the submitted ORSA supervisory report and the transmission evidence to the PRA as closure evidence.
Where the board defers its conclusion, reset the deadline from the new conclusion date and log the change with the minute reference.
checklist.done: the ORSA entry deadline runs from the signed board conclusion date and closes on transmission evidence.

checklist.step: Capture ad hoc PRA requests as calendar entries within one business day
actions: Monitor the shared regulatory correspondence mailbox and the BEEDS message function daily for PRA requests.
Create a calendar entry within one business day carrying the PRA-stated response date, the request reference and a named owner.
Where the stated date is not achievable, have the Head of Compliance request an extension in writing before the date, never after it.
Close the entry on the sent response and the acknowledgement, and file the correspondence thread.
checklist.done: every PRA request has a calendar entry within one business day and closes on evidenced response and acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Produce the monthly timeliness dashboard
actions: Build the dashboard from the obligations register: entries due, closed on time, closed late, open past deadline, and average margin in business days.
Split by obligation type — quarterly return, annual return, SFCR, ORSA, ad hoc — so a single weak process is visible.
Include the trend of entries closed with under 3 business days of margin as an early warning of process strain.
Circulate to the Chief Financial Officer, Chief Risk Officer and Head of Compliance on the first working day of each month.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard showing on-time rate, overdue entries and margin trend by obligation type is circulated to the named executives.

checklist.step: Run a quarterly calendar completeness challenge
actions: Take the PRA reporting requirement list for the entity and tick off each requirement against a calendar entry.
Ask the Statutory Reporting Manager, the Chief Actuary and the Chief Risk Officer to name any regulatory deliverable they produce that is not on the calendar.
Create entries for anything named and record why it was missing.
Minute the challenge and its outcome at the compliance committee.
checklist.done: the quarterly challenge is minuted with an entry created for every deliverable named as missing.

checklist.step: Handle a missed or late filing as a breach, not a slip
actions: Raise a breach record within one business day of discovery with the obligation, the deadline, the actual date and the days late.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether the PRA must be notified and record the reasoning either way.
Where notification is required, have the Chief Risk Officer send it to the supervision contact with the cause and the control fix and its date.
Present the breach and the fix to the board Risk Committee at its next meeting.
checklist.done: every late filing has a breach record within one business day, a documented notification decision and a committee report.

checklist.step: Test the calendar against a leave and handover scenario
actions: Pick one quarterly return cycle and run it with the named owner formally unavailable, using the deputy only.
Check the deputy receives the reminder ladder, can access the reporting engine and BEEDS, and holds the procedure document.
Record any access or knowledge gap found and fix it before the next cycle.
Document the exercise and its findings in the register against the affected entries.
checklist.done: a deputy-only run is completed with every access and knowledge gap recorded and fixed before the next cycle.

checklist.step: Recalculate the calendar whenever a deadline rule changes
actions: On any PRA policy statement affecting reporting deadlines, identify every affected entry and the first reference date the change applies from.
Recompute the affected dates, update the stored derivation text and the source reference, and notify the owners of the change.
Retire entries for templates or returns removed by the change, recording the retirement reason and the authority for it.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the recalculated set before it goes live.
checklist.done: every rule change produces recomputed dates, updated derivations, retired obsolete entries and a Head of Compliance approval.

checklist.step: Archive the closed calendar period
actions: At each quarter end, export the closed entries with their derivations, deadlines, actual dates, margins, approvers and evidence links.
File the export under REG-023/Calendar/<quarter> and apply the 10-year retention label.
Confirm the evidence links resolve from the archive copy, replacing any link that points only to a live system.
Index by obligation type, reference date and owner.
checklist.done: the quarter's closed entries are archived with resolvable evidence, a 10-year label and an obligation-type index.

testing.step: Build the population from both the calendar and the regulator's records
actions: Extract every obligations register entry with a due date inside the quarter, with owner, derivation, deadline, closure date and evidence link.
Extract independently from the BEEDS portal every submission made for the entity in the quarter with its timestamp and reference number.
Extract the website publication log for any disclosure published in the quarter.
Combine into a single population so entries with no submission and submissions with no entry both appear.
testing.done: the population is built from register, BEEDS and publication log so both directions of gap are visible.

testing.step: Reconcile calendar entries to actual submissions in both directions
actions: Match each register entry to a BEEDS submission or publication record on obligation and reference date.
List entries closed with no matching submission record — these are closures on assertion.
List submissions with no register entry — these are filings made outside the control.
Treat both lists as automatic exceptions and quantify them before sampling.
testing.done: both unmatched lists are produced and logged as exceptions with no judgemental filtering.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of calendar entries
actions: Take 100% of entries for the quarterly return, the annual return, the SFCR and the ORSA because a miss on any of them is material.
Take 20 further entries at random with a recorded seed from ad hoc requests and notification obligations.
Take 100% of entries closed with a margin under 3 business days.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all major returns and all thin-margin closures is documented.

testing.step: Re-derive the stored deadline from the current rule
actions: For each sampled entry, open the PRA Rulebook Reporting Part or the cited policy statement and read the deadline rule as it stands.
Recompute the deadline from the reference date using the England and Wales business-day calendar and list the holidays applied.
Compare to the deadline stored on the entry and to the derivation text.
Treat a right date with a wrong or missing derivation as a fail, because it will not survive the next rule change.
testing.done: each sampled deadline re-derives from the current rule and the stored derivation text matches the recomputation.

testing.step: Re-perform the timeliness calculation from primary evidence
actions: Take the submission timestamp from the BEEDS receipt or the publication timestamp from the web server log, not from the register field.
Recompute the margin in business days against the re-derived deadline and compare to the margin recorded on the entry.
Confirm the evidence attached to the entry is the actual receipt or URL capture and not a screenshot of the register itself.
Log any entry where the recomputed margin is negative as a reportable breach.
testing.done: every sampled margin recomputes from primary evidence and any negative margin is reported as a breach.

testing.step: Test calendar completeness against the regulatory requirement list
actions: Build an independent list of the entity's PRA reporting, disclosure and notification obligations from the Rulebook and the current policy statements.
Tick each against a register entry and list any obligation with no entry at all.
Interview the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Chief Actuary for regulatory deliverables produced outside the register.
Log every obligation with no entry as a completeness exception naming who produces it today.
testing.done: an independently built obligation list is fully mapped to register entries or every gap is named with its current producer.

testing.step: Test the reminder ladder and escalation actually fired
actions: Pull the notification audit log for each sampled entry and confirm alerts were sent at T-30, T-15, T-5 and T-1 to the owner and deputy.
Confirm the status moved to amber and red where draft evidence was absent at the configured points.
For any entry that went overdue, confirm the daily page to the Head of Compliance was delivered.
Log configured-but-not-fired alerts as a control failure separate from any late filing.
testing.done: the notification log evidences the full alert ladder and escalation for each sampled entry.

testing.step: Test ownership, deputisation and leaver handling
actions: Take the leaver and internal-mover list for the quarter from the HRIS and cross-check against register owner and deputy fields.
Confirm every entry owned or deputised by a leaver was reassigned within 5 business days of the leave date.
Confirm no entry has the same person as owner and deputy, and that the deputy sits in a different team.
Log orphaned or self-deputised entries as control failures.
testing.done: no entry is orphaned or self-deputised and every leaver reassignment happened within 5 business days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the obligation, the deadline, the actual date and the days late or the missing evidence.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: date rolled forward not recomputed, obligation never registered, evidence not attached at closure, owner left, alert misconfigured, extension not requested in time.
Name an owner and a remediation date and require the calendar configuration change to be evidenced, not promised.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue id, root cause, owner, remediation date and an evidenced configuration fix.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time rate and the evidence-attached rate and compare to the zero-late and zero-unevidenced thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the two-way reconciliation and the deadline re-derivations.
Have the reviewer — who owns and deputises on no calendar entry and cannot edit the register — sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any late filing to the board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with on-time and evidence rates, a stated conclusion and a Risk Committee reporting date is filed.

checklist.step: Identify the important business services for the UK entity
actions: Apply the identification criteria — harm to policyholders and risk to the safety and soundness of the firm — to each end-to-end service rather than to internal processes.

Take the candidate list to the Risk Committee: annuity payment, policyholder servicing and claims settlement, new business and premium collection, investment and settlement, and Solvency UK regulatory reporting.
Record for each service the customer outcome it delivers and the harm that arises if it stops, quantified where possible in policyholders affected per day.
Have the board approve the final list and record the approval date on each service record in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: a board-approved important business service list exists with a quantified harm statement per service.

checklist.step: Set and approve an impact tolerance for each important business service
actions: For each service, express the impact tolerance as the maximum tolerable duration of disruption, with any secondary metric such as volume of missed annuity payments.
Base the tolerance on the point at which policyholder harm becomes intolerable, not on what the current infrastructure can achieve.
Document the assumptions, the data used and the dissenting views raised at the Risk Committee.
Obtain board approval and record the tolerance, its approval date and its owner against the service.
checklist.done: every important business service carries a board-approved impact tolerance expressed as a maximum tolerable duration with recorded assumptions.

checklist.step: Map the end-to-end dependencies of each service
actions: For each service map the people, processes, premises, technology, data and third parties needed to deliver it, taking the application and infrastructure layer from the CMDB.
Follow the chain through to the underlying hosting, network and data flows rather than stopping at the front-end application.
Mark each dependency critical or non-critical based on whether its loss stops the service inside the impact tolerance.
Have the service owner confirm the map is complete in writing and record the confirmation date.
checklist.done: each service has a confirmed end-to-end dependency map with criticality marked and CMDB references on the technology layer.

checklist.step: Run the business impact analysis and set recovery objectives
actions: For each critical dependency determine the recovery time objective and the recovery point objective, taking the technology figures from the Disaster Recovery Manager.
Aggregate the dependency objectives into a service-level recovery time and compare it to the approved impact tolerance.
Where the aggregated recovery time exceeds the tolerance, record the gap in hours and raise a remediation issue rather than adjusting the tolerance.
Record peak periods — annuity payment run dates, quarter-end reporting — when the tolerance is tightest.
checklist.done: each service has an aggregated recovery time compared to its tolerance, with every gap quantified in hours and raised as an issue.

checklist.step: Write or refresh the continuity plan for each service
actions: Use the standard plan template: scope, invocation criteria and authority, roles with named individuals and deputies, workaround procedures per critical dependency, communications tree, and stand-down criteria.
Write the manual workaround for each critical dependency in enough detail that an unfamiliar colleague could run it — which forms, which spreadsheet, which authorisation limit applies.
Include the sequence and priority for restoring services when several are down at once.
Version the plan, name the owner and set the next review date twelve months out.
checklist.done: every service has a versioned plan with named roles, per-dependency workarounds, restoration priority and a dated next review.

checklist.step: Document the continuity arrangements for annuity payment specifically
actions: Record the payment run calendar, the cut-off times, the bank file format and the approval limits used in the normal annuity payment process.
Write the contingency route: a pre-agreed manual payment file, the standby bank channel, the authorisation chain and the maximum batch size the manual route can handle per day.
Agree the standby arrangements with the Treasury Manager and the bank in writing, and record the contact and the activation reference.
State how policyholders are told about a delayed payment and who authorises the communication.
checklist.done: the annuity payment plan states a tested contingency payment route with agreed bank arrangements, daily capacity and a policyholder communication trigger.

checklist.step: Document continuity for Solvency UK regulatory reporting
actions: Record the dependencies for the reporting service: the general ledger, the actuarial platform, the reporting engine, the XBRL build and the BEEDS portal.
Write the contingency for each: an offline data extract, a prior-version model run, a manual template build and an alternative BEEDS submitter with active credentials.
State the point at which a disruption makes the 30 or 70 business day deadline unachievable and who requests an extension from the PRA.
Keep a current list of authorised BEEDS users so a single unavailable submitter cannot stop a filing.
checklist.done: the reporting continuity plan names a workaround per dependency, a deadline-breach trigger point and at least two active BEEDS submitters.

checklist.step: Cover third-party and outsourced dependencies in the plans
actions: For each critical third party supporting an important business service, obtain their continuity and exit arrangements and their stated recovery times.
Check the contract carries continuity, testing participation and notification obligations, and log the clause reference on the dependency record.
Record the substitutability of each provider and the realistic time to move, not the contractual notice period.
Raise an issue where a provider's recovery time exceeds what the service tolerance can absorb.
checklist.done: every critical third party has documented recovery times, a contract clause reference and a realistic substitution assessment.

checklist.step: Keep the call trees and contact data current
actions: Refresh plan contact details quarterly from the HRIS, including personal mobile numbers held under the emergency contact consent.
Remove leavers within 5 business days of the HRIS leave date and appoint a replacement on the plan the same week.
Send a no-reply-required test message through the mass notification route each quarter and record the delivery rate.
Investigate every undelivered contact and correct the record.
checklist.done: contact data is refreshed quarterly, leavers are removed within 5 business days and the notification test delivery rate is recorded.

checklist.step: Run the annual policy review
actions: Review the policy against Conditions Governing Business 2.4 and the current PRA operational resilience expectations, marking each requirement to a policy clause.
Fold in lessons from the year: invocations, test findings, incidents, audit findings and outsourcing changes.
Update the important business service list and the tolerances where the business has changed materially.
Circulate the draft to the Chief Operating Officer, Chief Risk Officer, Head of IT and Head of Compliance for comment before the committee.
checklist.done: the reviewed policy maps each requirement to a clause and incorporates the year's lessons, with comments from all four named executives.

checklist.step: Produce the operational resilience self-assessment
actions: Document for each important business service: the tolerance, the mapping, the scenario testing done, whether the firm can stay within tolerance, and the vulnerabilities found.
State plainly where the firm cannot yet remain within tolerance, with the remediation plan and completion date.
Include the lessons-learned actions from the year's testing and any live incidents.
Have the board approve the self-assessment and record the approval date.
checklist.done: a board-approved self-assessment states per service whether the firm can remain within tolerance, with dated remediation for every gap.

checklist.step: Take the policy and self-assessment to the board
actions: Load the policy, the important business service list with tolerances, the self-assessment and the open gap register into the board portal 5 business days before the meeting.
Present the gaps where recovery time exceeds tolerance as a decision item requiring either investment or an explicit risk acceptance.
Minute the approval of the policy, the tolerances and any risk acceptance with its expiry date.
Circulate the minute reference to the Business Continuity Manager for the plan records.
checklist.done: the board has approved the policy and tolerances and explicitly accepted or funded each recovery-time gap, with the decision minuted.

checklist.step: Collect plan owner attestations
actions: Issue an attestation task in the GRC platform to each plan owner within 20 business days of the policy approval date.
Require the owner to confirm the roles, contacts, workarounds and dependency list are current as at a stated date, not merely that the plan exists.
Chase non-responders at 10 and 3 business days before the due date and escalate outstanding attestations to the Chief Operating Officer.
Record the attestation date and the attesting individual on each plan record.
checklist.done: every plan carries a dated owner attestation covering roles, contacts, workarounds and dependencies.

checklist.step: Feed the continuity position into the ORSA and the SFCR
actions: Supply the ORSA operational risk section with the tolerance breaches, the open gaps and the scenario testing outcomes.
Supply SFCR Section B.4 with a description of the continuity arrangements consistent with the board-approved policy.
Confirm the operational risk capital assessment reflects any material unremediated continuity gap.
Record the cross-references so a PRA reviewer can move between the ORSA, the SFCR and the self-assessment.
checklist.done: the ORSA and SFCR Section B.4 carry a continuity description consistent with the approved policy and the open gap register.

checklist.step: Archive the superseded policy and plan versions
actions: File the approved policy version, the service list, tolerances, business impact analyses, plans, attestations and the board minute under REG-023/Continuity/<year>.
Apply the 7-year-from-supersession retention label to the superseded versions and keep the current version live in the GRC platform.
Index by important business service, version and board approval date.
Confirm a reader can reconstruct what the arrangements were at any past date from the archive alone.
checklist.done: superseded versions are archived under a 7-year label and the arrangements at any past date can be reconstructed from the archive.

testing.step: Build the population of services, plans and dependencies
actions: Extract the board-approved important business service list with tolerances, approval dates and owners.
Extract every business continuity plan with its version, owner, last review date and attestation date.
Extract every mapped dependency with its criticality flag, recovery time objective and workaround reference.
Reconcile the plan count to the service list so no service is left without a plan and no plan is orphaned.
testing.done: services, plans and dependencies are extracted and reconciled with no service unplanned and no plan orphaned.

testing.step: Reconcile the service list to the actual business
actions: Take the entity's product and operations inventory and the SFCR Section A description of material lines of business.
Check each material customer-facing service appears on the important business service list or has a recorded rationale for exclusion.
Test the exclusion rationale against the harm criteria rather than accepting a management judgement.
Log any material service absent from the list as a completeness exception to the Risk Committee.
testing.done: every material customer-facing service is on the list or has a harm-tested exclusion rationale on file.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of important business services and their plans because the population is small and each is material.
Take 25 critical dependencies at random with a recorded seed across the services, weighted to third-party and technology dependencies.
Take 100% of dependencies whose recovery time objective exceeds the service tolerance.
Record the seed, the population sizes and the extract date in the workpaper.
testing.done: all services and a reproducible dependency sample including every tolerance-exceeding dependency are documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the tolerance versus recovery time comparison
actions: For each service, rebuild the aggregated recovery time from the sampled dependency recovery time objectives rather than reading the reported figure.
Take the technology recovery figures independently from the Disaster Recovery Manager's current capability record, not from the plan.
Compare the rebuilt recovery time to the board-approved tolerance and record the gap in hours.
Log any service where the reported position understates the rebuilt gap as an exception naming who reported it.
testing.done: each service's recovery time is rebuilt from source capability data and compared to the approved tolerance with the gap in hours.

testing.step: Test plan currency, attestation and reviewer independence
actions: For each plan, compare the last review date to the twelve-month review cycle and compute days overdue where applicable.
Confirm the attestation is dated within 20 business days of the policy approval and covers roles, contacts, workarounds and dependencies rather than plan existence.
Confirm the attester is the recorded plan owner and is still employed per the HRIS.
Log plans past review, generic attestations and attestations by leavers as exceptions.
testing.done: every plan is within its review cycle with a specific, current-owner attestation, or the failure is logged with days overdue.

testing.step: Trace named workarounds to something that actually exists
actions: For each sampled critical dependency, open the referenced workaround and confirm the named form, spreadsheet, standby channel or manual procedure exists and is accessible offline.
For the annuity payment contingency, confirm the standby bank arrangement is documented in writing by the Treasury Manager and the activation reference is current.
For the reporting contingency, confirm at least two BEEDS submitter credentials are active by checking the portal user list.
Log any workaround that is a description with no underlying artefact as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled workaround resolves to an existing, accessible artefact or credential, or is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Test third-party dependency coverage against the contracts
actions: For each sampled third-party dependency, open the executed contract and locate the continuity, testing participation, notification and exit clauses.
Compare the provider's contractual recovery commitment to the recovery time recorded on the dependency map.
Confirm the provider's most recent continuity test evidence is on file and dated within the last twelve months.
Log dependencies where the contract carries no continuity obligation as exceptions to the Chief Operating Officer.
testing.done: each sampled third-party dependency has a located contract clause, a matching recovery commitment and current test evidence.

testing.step: Test contact data accuracy by live verification
actions: Draw 30 contact records at random from the sampled plans and compare each to the HRIS record for employment status and role.
Send an unannounced test notification through the mass notification route and record the delivery and acknowledgement rate within 30 minutes.
Compare the leaver list for the quarter to the plan contact fields and count records not removed within 5 business days.
Log every stale contact with the plan it sits on and the days it has been wrong.
testing.done: contact accuracy is measured against the HRIS and a live notification test, with stale records counted and aged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the service, the plan or the dependency and the gap quantified in hours or records.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: tolerance never approved, dependency map incomplete, recovery capability overstated, workaround artefact missing, contract lacks continuity clause, contacts stale.
Name an owner and a remediation date and require evidence of the fix rather than a plan update alone.
Escalate any service that cannot remain within its tolerance to the Chief Operating Officer for a funded plan or a dated risk acceptance.
testing.done: every exception has an issue id, a quantified gap, a root cause, an owner and a remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the proportion of services able to remain within tolerance and the plan currency rate, and compare to the zero-overdue-plan and zero-unapproved-tolerance thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective against Conditions Governing Business 2.4.
Have the reviewer — who owns no continuity plan and sits in second line — sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and every unremediated tolerance gap to the board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the within-tolerance proportion, plan currency rate and a conclusion against CGB 2.4 is filed and reported.
