checklist.step: Build the annual test calendar with coverage per important business service
actions: Take the board-approved important business service list and map each service to the platforms that deliver it using the dependency maps.
Schedule at least one severe but plausible scenario test per service inside the twelve months to 30 September, avoiding the annuity payment run dates and the quarter-end reporting windows.

Assign each test a platform owner, a test manager, a business observer and a scenario from the library: data centre loss, third-party outage, ransomware with data corruption, or key person and premises loss.
Raise a change record per test in the ITSM platform with the window, the systems in scope and the rollback plan.
checklist.done: every important business service has at least one scheduled test with a named scenario, owners and a raised change record.

checklist.step: Write the scenario script with entry, exit and abort criteria
actions: Write the scenario narrative: what fails, at what time, and what the business sees, expressed from the customer's position rather than the server's.
Set the entry criteria — backups verified, change freeze in place, participants briefed — and the exit criteria — service restored, data reconciled, tolerance assessed.
Set the abort criteria and name who can call an abort, and record that an abort is recorded as a failed test rather than a cancelled one.
Circulate the script to the platform owner, the business observer and the Head of Compliance at least 10 business days before the window.
checklist.done: the script states the scenario, entry, exit and abort criteria with a named abort authority and is circulated 10 business days ahead.

checklist.step: Verify backups and replication state before the test
actions: Confirm the last successful backup for every in-scope database, its completion timestamp and its verified restore status.
Confirm replication lag between primary and secondary sites is inside the recovery point objective at the moment the test starts, and record the measured lag.
Take a pre-test record count and control total for the key tables — policies in force, annuity payment instructions, ledger balances — for the post-test reconciliation.
Refuse to start the test if replication lag exceeds the recovery point objective, and record the refusal as a finding.
checklist.done: backup status, measured replication lag and pre-test control totals are recorded before the scenario begins.

checklist.step: Execute the failover and timestamp every step
actions: Start the clock at the declared point of failure and log a timestamp against every step: detection, declaration, invocation decision, failover start, service availability, business verification.
Fail over the in-scope platforms to the secondary site following the runbook, and record every deviation from the runbook as it happens rather than afterwards.
Capture the monitoring dashboards at each milestone showing service health, replication state and transaction throughput.
Record the measured recovery time from declaration to business-verified availability.
checklist.done: a timestamped execution log with dashboard captures records every step and yields a measured recovery time.

checklist.step: Have the business verify the service, not just the infrastructure
actions: With the platform back, run a scripted set of real business transactions: retrieve an annuity policy, process a payment instruction, record a servicing change, produce a statement.
Compare the results to expected values prepared before the test and record each pass or fail against the transaction.
Confirm interfaces to the general ledger, the payment gateway and the document repository are working, not only that the application screen loads.
Declare the service restored only when the business verification set passes, and record who declared it and when.
checklist.done: a scripted business transaction set passes and a named business owner has declared the service restored at a recorded time.

checklist.step: Reconcile data integrity after failover
actions: Re-take the record counts and control totals for the key tables and compare to the pre-test figures.
Identify every transaction submitted during the outage window and confirm it is either present or in the documented replay queue.
Compute the actual data loss in records and in elapsed time and compare it to the recovery point objective.
Investigate every unexplained difference to root cause; an unexplained difference of any size fails the test.
checklist.done: post-test control totals reconcile to pre-test figures, actual data loss is quantified against the recovery point objective, and no difference is unexplained.

checklist.step: Exercise the manual workaround in the same test
actions: During the outage window, run the plan's manual workaround for the affected service rather than waiting for the system to come back.
Measure how many transactions the workaround processed per hour and compare it to the normal daily volume for the service.
Record where the workaround broke down — missing form, unavailable authorisation, unreachable contact — with the exact step.
Feed every breakdown into the continuity plan update as a specific text change, not a general observation.
checklist.done: the workaround is run under outage conditions with measured throughput and every breakdown recorded as a specific plan change.

checklist.step: Test the third-party leg of the scenario
actions: For scenarios involving a critical provider, invoke the contractual test participation clause and agree the provider's role in the exercise in writing.
Where the provider will not participate, obtain their own most recent test report and assess whether it covers the firm's service and recovery times.
Record the provider's measured or attested recovery time against the dependency map figure.
Raise an issue where the provider neither participates nor evidences a comparable test.
checklist.done: each critical provider in scope either participated or supplied a current test report assessed against the firm's recovery times.

checklist.step: Fail back to primary and prove the return path
actions: Execute the documented failback to the primary site inside the agreed window and log the timestamps.
Re-run the data integrity reconciliation after failback because the return path breaks data as often as the outbound path.
Confirm replication is re-established and lag is back inside the recovery point objective before closing the change record.
Record any manual step required during failback that is not in the runbook.
checklist.done: failback completes with reconciled data, restored replication inside the recovery point objective, and undocumented manual steps recorded.

checklist.step: Judge the result against the impact tolerance
actions: Compare the measured recovery time to the platform recovery time objective and to the service impact tolerance.
Assess the customer impact that would have occurred: annuity payments missed, servicing requests unanswered, reporting deadline days consumed.
Record the test as passed only if the service stayed inside the impact tolerance and the exit criteria were met; anything else is a fail with the breach quantified.
Where the reporting service was tested, state explicitly whether the 30 or 70 business day deadline would still have been met.
checklist.done: the test carries a pass or fail judgement against the impact tolerance with the breach quantified in time and customer impact.

checklist.step: Write the test report within 15 business days
actions: Write the report covering scenario, participants, timeline with timestamps, measured recovery time and data loss, business verification results, tolerance judgement and findings.
State the findings plainly, including the ones that make the programme look bad — an unrecorded manual step or an unreachable contact is the point of the exercise.
Have the platform owner, the business observer and the Operational Resilience Lead review and sign the report.
Issue within 15 business days of the test date and file it against the test record.
checklist.done: a signed test report with timestamps, measured metrics and a tolerance judgement is issued within 15 business days.

checklist.step: Raise lessons-learned actions with owners inside 10 business days
actions: Raise one action per finding in the ITSM platform with the finding text, a named owner and a due date proportionate to the risk.
Distinguish runbook corrections, capability investments and plan text changes so they route to the right owner.
Set actions arising from a tolerance breach to the highest priority with executive visibility.
Confirm every action has an owner within 10 business days of the test report.
checklist.done: every finding has an ITSM action with an owner and a due date within 10 business days of the report.

checklist.step: Retest what failed rather than closing on a fix description
actions: For any test that breached its tolerance, schedule a retest of the failed component within the remediation due date, not at the next annual cycle.
Require the retest to use the same scenario and the same measurement points so results are comparable.
Close the original finding only on the retest evidence, with the Chief Information Officer signing the closure.
Where a retest is not possible before year end, record the residual risk and take it to the Risk Committee for acceptance.
checklist.done: every tolerance breach has a comparable retest or a Risk Committee residual risk acceptance, with CIO-signed closure.

checklist.step: Report programme results to the board and into the self-assessment
actions: Present the annual programme to the Risk Committee: services tested, tolerance breaches, measured recovery times against objectives, and open remediation.
Supply the operational resilience self-assessment with the test evidence per important business service.
Supply the ORSA operational risk section with the breaches and the residual exposure.
Minute the committee's view on whether the firm can remain within its tolerances on the current evidence.
checklist.done: the programme is reported to the Risk Committee, feeds the self-assessment and the ORSA, and the committee's tolerance view is minuted.

checklist.step: Archive the test evidence for 7 years
actions: File the test plan, scenario script, execution log, dashboard captures, business verification results, data reconciliation, report and closure evidence under REG-023/Resilience-Testing/<year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the test date and lock the folder.
Index by important business service, scenario type, test date and pass or fail outcome.
Confirm the execution logs are retained in a readable form independent of the monitoring tool's own retention period.
checklist.done: the test pack is archived for 7 years, indexed by service and outcome, with logs readable outside the monitoring tool.

testing.step: Build the population of scheduled and executed tests
actions: Extract the annual test calendar with every scheduled test, its service, scenario, window and owner.
Extract every executed test change record with its actual start and end timestamps and completion status.
Extract every lessons-learned action raised in the year with owner, due date and status.
Reconcile scheduled to executed and list scheduled tests with no execution record before sampling.
testing.done: scheduled and executed tests are reconciled and every unexecuted scheduled test is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile test coverage to the important business service list
actions: Take the board-approved important business service list independently from the GRC platform.
Map each executed test to the services it covered using the dependency maps, not the test title.
List any service with no covering test inside the twelve months to 30 September.
Treat partial coverage — a platform tested but not the end-to-end service — as untested and log it.
testing.done: every important business service is mapped to a covering executed test or logged as untested with the coverage gap described.

testing.step: Draw and document the test sample
actions: Take 100% of tests covering annuity payment and Solvency UK regulatory reporting because a failure there is directly regulatory.
Take 100% of tests recorded as failed or aborted.
Take 8 further tests at random with a recorded seed from the remainder.
Record the seed, the population size and the extract date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all regulatory-critical and all failed tests is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the recovery time measurement from the raw logs
actions: Pull the raw system and application logs for each sampled test window rather than relying on the execution log the team wrote.
Identify the declared failure timestamp and the first successful business transaction timestamp on the secondary site.
Recompute the recovery time from those two points and compare to the reported figure.
Log any reported recovery time shorter than the log-derived figure as an exception naming the reporter.
testing.done: each sampled recovery time is recomputed from raw logs and reconciled to the reported figure.

testing.step: Re-perform the data integrity reconciliation
actions: Take the pre-test and post-test control totals from the archived evidence and re-run the same counts against the retained database snapshots.
Recompute the record-level data loss and the elapsed data loss window and compare both to the recovery point objective.
Confirm every transaction in the documented replay queue was actually replayed by checking for its presence in the current data.
Log any difference the original reconciliation reported as explained but which has no supporting explanation on file.
testing.done: data loss is recomputed against the recovery point objective and every replayed transaction is confirmed present.

testing.step: Test the tolerance judgement against the approved tolerance
actions: Take the board-approved impact tolerance for each sampled service as at the test date, from the board minute rather than the current record.
Compare the log-derived recovery time to that tolerance and reach an independent pass or fail judgement.
For the reporting service test, recompute whether the 30 or 70 business day deadline would still have been met given the days consumed.
Log any test reported as passed that fails on the independent judgement as a significant exception to the Risk Committee.
testing.done: each sampled test carries an independent pass or fail judgement against the tolerance approved at the test date.

testing.step: Trace the business verification and workaround evidence
actions: For each sampled test, open the business verification results and confirm real transactions were run with expected values prepared in advance.
Confirm the named business owner's restoration declaration exists with a timestamp, and is not the same person who executed the failover.
Confirm the manual workaround was actually exercised, with measured throughput recorded, rather than assumed available.
Log tests where only infrastructure health was verified as a fail on the exit criteria.
testing.done: each sampled test evidences real business transactions, a segregated restoration declaration and a measured workaround run.

testing.step: Age the remediation actions and test closure evidence
actions: Compute days overdue for every open lessons-learned action against its due date and bucket by age.
For each closed action, open the closure evidence and judge whether it demonstrates the fix works — a retest result, an updated runbook with a change record, a configuration diff.
Reject closures supported by an owner statement alone and reopen them.
Confirm every tolerance-breach finding was closed on a comparable retest signed by the Chief Information Officer.
testing.done: open actions are aged and every closed action has operational closure evidence, with breach findings closed only on a signed retest.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the test, the service, the metric and the difference between reported and re-performed values.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: test not scheduled, test aborted and recorded as cancelled, recovery time measured from the wrong point, data loss unexplained, workaround not exercised, action closed without evidence.
Name an owner and a remediation date and require a retest rather than a document update where the capability itself failed.
Escalate any service with no covering test to the Chief Operating Officer within one business day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue id, a quantified difference, a root cause, an owner and a remediation or retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the coverage rate across important business services and the pass rate against impact tolerances on the independent judgement.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective on the resilience testing control.
Have the reviewer — who sits outside infrastructure and executed no sampled test — sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any untested service and any unremediated tolerance breach to the board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating coverage rate, independent pass rate and a conclusion is filed and reported to the Risk Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the outsourcing and third-party register and the ICT dependency register for the UK entity; the compliance function assessment of the register sits with the Head of Compliance under the compliance key function duty

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook, Conditions Governing Business 4 (compliance function advising the board on regulatory compliance and assessing regulatory change) read with the PRA outsourcing and third party risk expectations requiring a register of all outsourcing arrangements and the critical third party oversight regime for services underpinning important business services

In-scope processes.value: Continuous maintenance of the outsourcing and ICT third-party register for the UK entity: onboarding due diligence, materiality classification, PRA pre-notification of material outsourcing, contract clause coverage, ongoing monitoring, concentration and substitutability assessment, and exit planning

In-scope systems.value: The register, materiality assessments, monitoring records and exit plans are held in the GRC platform, linked to the executed contracts in the contract lifecycle management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Third Party and Outsourcing Register Procedure RSK-TPR-02 — the register data model, the materiality decision tree, the PRA pre-notification trigger and lead time, the mandatory contract clause checklist, the annual re-assessment cycle and the exit plan standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer with the Head of Compliance; reviewed annually and on any PRA policy statement affecting outsourcing, third party risk or the critical third party regime

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: PRA pre-notification of a new material outsourcing arrangement or a material change is sent at least 6 weeks before the arrangement is entered into or altered; the full register is re-attested annually by 30 September; register entries must be created within 10 business days of contract signature

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC alerts fire to the relationship owner 90, 60 and 30 days before each material contract renewal or expiry, at the annual re-assessment due date, and on any monitoring report overdue by 10 business days; unregistered signed contracts page the Third-Party Risk Manager weekly

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Register entries with their version history, due diligence packs, materiality assessments, PRA pre-notifications and acknowledgements, contract clause checklists, monitoring reports and exit plans retained 7 years from the end of the arrangement

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A signed arrangement absent from the register, a material outsourcing entered without PRA pre-notification, a missing mandatory contract clause or an overdue re-assessment is raised as a compliance issue with an owner and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Risk Officer signs off closure of every material outsourcing register defect and approves any decision to continue an arrangement with a missing mandatory clause

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every register entry live at the test date, every third-party contract signed in the period taken from the procurement and contract systems, and every supplier paid in the period taken from the accounts payable ledger

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero material outsourcing arrangements missing from the register; zero material arrangements entered without a PRA pre-notification at least 6 weeks ahead; every material entry must carry all mandatory contract clauses, a current monitoring report and an exit plan; any entry past its annual re-assessment date is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous; the test runs quarterly on newly signed and newly classified arrangements and annually across the whole register before the September re-attestation

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must hold no relationship ownership on the register and must not sit in procurement or vendor management

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly and annual third-party register testing workpaper (register population, three-way reconciliation to contracts and payments, clause coverage testing, notification recomputation, exception log) filed under REG-023/Third-Party/<period>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The register extract in the expected field set, the material arrangement list with pre-notification evidence, contract clause coverage summaries, concentration analysis and exit plans, producible to the PRA within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer answers PRA questions on outsourcing and third-party arrangements with the Head of Compliance; an arrangement found to have been entered without pre-notification is self-reported to the supervision contact with the cause and the register control fix

checklist.step: Define the register data model against the PRA field expectations
actions: Configure the register to hold per arrangement: provider legal name and LEI, group parent, service description, whether it is outsourcing, whether it is material or critical, the important business services it supports, start and end dates, notice period, country of service provision and data location, sub-outsourcers, annual cost and the relationship owner.
Add ICT-specific fields for technology arrangements: hosting model, data classification handled, network connectivity type, and whether the provider holds privileged access.
Make provider LEI, materiality and supported important business service mandatory so an entry cannot be saved half-built.
Have the Head of Compliance confirm the field set covers what the PRA expects to see on request.
checklist.done: the register enforces the full field set with materiality and supported service mandatory, confirmed by the compliance function.

checklist.step: Sweep the existing supplier estate into the register
actions: Extract every supplier with spend in the last 24 months from the procurement system and the accounts payable ledger, with amounts and cost centres.
Screen out pure goods purchases and identify every arrangement where a provider performs a process, service or activity the firm would otherwise perform itself.
Match each identified arrangement to a register entry and list the unmatched ones for onboarding.
Hand the unmatched list to the Third-Party Risk Manager with the spend figure and the internal sponsor for each.
checklist.done: the supplier estate is screened and every service arrangement is either matched to a register entry or listed for onboarding with a named sponsor.

checklist.step: Classify each arrangement as outsourcing and assess materiality
actions: Apply the outsourcing test: is the provider performing on a continuing basis a process, service or activity that the firm would otherwise carry out itself.

Apply the materiality decision tree — effect on important business services, on policyholder outcomes, on the firm's ability to meet regulatory obligations, on financial soundness, and the difficulty of substitution.
Record the answer to each decision tree question with its evidence, not just the resulting classification.
Have the Chief Risk Officer approve every material classification and every decision that a technology arrangement is not material.
checklist.done: each arrangement carries a documented outsourcing test and a materiality assessment with per-question evidence and CRO approval where material.

checklist.step: Run due diligence before a material arrangement is entered
actions: Collect the provider's audited financial statements, ownership structure, insurance cover, security certifications and most recent independent assurance report.
Assess the provider's own continuity and disaster recovery capability against the recovery times the supported important business service needs.
Identify the sub-outsourcers the provider relies on for the service and record them on the register entry.
Record the due diligence conclusion with any conditions the contract must carry, and route it to the Chief Risk Officer for material arrangements.
checklist.done: each material arrangement has a due diligence pack covering finances, security, continuity capability and named sub-outsourcers, with a recorded conclusion.

checklist.step: Pre-notify the PRA of material outsourcing at least 6 weeks ahead
actions: As soon as a material classification is approved, prepare the notification covering the service, the provider, the countries involved, the supported important business services and the risk assessment conclusion.
Send it to the named PRA supervision contact at least 6 weeks before the arrangement is entered into or materially changed, and record the send date.
Log the PRA acknowledgement and any questions raised, and answer them before signature rather than after.
Block contract signature in the procurement workflow until the notification date plus 6 weeks has passed or the PRA confirms otherwise.
checklist.done: every material arrangement has a dated pre-notification at least 6 weeks before entry, with signature blocked until the period elapses.

checklist.step: Check the contract carries every mandatory clause before signature
actions: Run the mandatory clause checklist over the draft: audit and access rights for the firm and the PRA, data location and protection, sub-outsourcing consent and notification, service levels with remedies, security and incident notification timescales, continuity and testing participation, termination rights and exit assistance.
Record the clause reference — section and page — for each item rather than a yes flag.
Escalate any missing clause to Legal Counsel and the Chief Risk Officer before signature; a missing audit or exit clause blocks signature.
Attach the completed checklist to the register entry and link the executed contract.
checklist.done: each material contract has a clause checklist with a section reference per item and no blocking clause missing at signature.

checklist.step: Create or update the register entry within 10 business days of signature
actions: On contract execution, complete the register entry with every mandatory field and link the executed contract, the due diligence pack and the clause checklist.
Set the relationship owner, the annual re-assessment date and the renewal and expiry alert dates.
Record the supported important business services so the continuity dependency maps and the register stay consistent.
Report any entry not created within 10 business days of signature to the Third-Party Risk Manager weekly.
checklist.done: every executed arrangement has a complete, linked register entry within 10 business days of signature.

checklist.step: Build and maintain the ICT dependency view
actions: Map each ICT provider to the applications and infrastructure it supports using the CMDB, and record the configuration item references on the register entry.
Flag providers with privileged or administrative access to firm systems and cross-check against the identity platform's third-party account list.
Record where firm data is stored and processed by each ICT provider, including sub-processor locations.
Reconcile the ICT register entries to the CMDB quarterly and clear differences in both directions.
checklist.done: every ICT provider maps to CMDB configuration items, privileged access is flagged and reconciled to the identity platform, and data locations are recorded.

checklist.step: Assess concentration and substitutability across the register
actions: Group register entries by provider group to find where one group supports several important business services, and by service type to find single points of failure.
Identify providers whose failure would breach more than one impact tolerance and mark them as concentration risks.
For each material arrangement record the realistic time and cost to move to an alternative or bring the service in-house, evidenced by a named alternative rather than an assertion.
Report concentration risks to the Risk Committee with a recommendation on whether the exposure is within appetite.
checklist.done: provider-group concentration and per-arrangement substitutability are assessed with named alternatives and reported to the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Run ongoing monitoring against the service levels
actions: Collect the contractual service level reports at the agreed frequency and record actual performance against each measure on the register entry.
Obtain the provider's annual independent assurance report and read the exceptions and the complementary controls the firm is expected to operate.
Log every provider-side incident affecting the firm with its impact on the supported important business service and the notification timeliness against the contract.
Escalate persistent breaches through the contractual governance forum and record the outcome.
checklist.done: each material arrangement has current service level performance, a read assurance report with exceptions noted, and a logged incident history.

checklist.step: Maintain a documented and tested exit plan per material arrangement
actions: Write an exit plan per material arrangement covering trigger events, the target alternative, the data return format and timetable, the transition resource and the estimated cost and duration.
Include a stressed exit — provider insolvency or sudden withdrawal — not only an orderly contractual exit.
Confirm the exit assistance clause and the data return obligation in the contract support the plan, quoting the clause reference.
Review each plan annually and after any material change to the arrangement or the alternative market.
checklist.done: every material arrangement has an annually reviewed exit plan covering stressed exit, data return and a contract clause reference.

checklist.step: Run the annual re-assessment of every register entry
actions: Issue a re-assessment task to each relationship owner before the 30 September deadline covering materiality, supported services, sub-outsourcers, data locations and contract currency.
Require the owner to confirm each field as at a stated date and to attach the current service level and assurance evidence.
Re-run the materiality decision tree where the service, volume or supported business service has changed, and escalate any reclassification to material for CRO approval and PRA notification.
Escalate outstanding re-assessments to the Chief Risk Officer 10 business days before the deadline.
checklist.done: every register entry is re-attested by 30 September with evidence attached and every reclassification escalated.

checklist.step: Give the board a compliance function view of the third-party position
actions: Report to the board the register completeness rate, material arrangement count, notification compliance, clause gaps, concentration risks and open exit plan gaps.
Advise the board on the effect of regulatory change — critical third party oversight, data protection, operational resilience — on the current portfolio.
State plainly where the register cannot yet be relied on and what is being done about it.
Minute the board's consideration and any direction given.
checklist.done: the board has received a compliance function report on register completeness, notification compliance and regulatory change, and its consideration is minuted.

checklist.step: Handle a register defect or missed notification as a compliance breach
actions: Raise a compliance issue within one business day of discovering an unregistered material arrangement or a missed pre-notification.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether the PRA must be told now and record the reasoning either way.
Where notification is required, send it with the arrangement details, the reason it was missed and the register control fix with its date.
Report the breach and the fix to the Risk Committee at its next meeting.
checklist.done: every register defect has a compliance issue within one business day, a documented notification decision and a committee report.

checklist.step: Archive terminated arrangements and their evidence
actions: On termination, close the register entry with the exit date, confirmation that data was returned or destroyed, and the exit plan execution notes.
File the entry history, due diligence, notifications, clause checklist, monitoring reports and exit evidence under REG-023/Third-Party/<provider>.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the end of the arrangement and lock the folder.
Confirm the data return or destruction certificate from the provider is on file before closing the entry.
checklist.done: terminated arrangements are closed with a data return or destruction certificate and archived under a 7-year label.

testing.step: Build the population from register, contracts and payments
actions: Extract every live register entry with provider, materiality, supported important business services, re-assessment date and relationship owner.
Extract every third-party contract executed in the period from the contract lifecycle management repository.
Extract every supplier paid in the period from the accounts payable ledger with amounts and cost centres.
Combine into one population keyed on provider so arrangements present in any one source but absent from the register are visible.
testing.done: a three-source population is built and every provider present in contracts or payments but absent from the register is visible.

testing.step: Reconcile the register three ways and list the gaps
actions: Match register entries to executed contracts and to paid suppliers, allowing for provider name variants by matching on LEI and bank details where names differ.
List paid service providers with no register entry, executed service contracts with no register entry, and register entries with no contract on file.
Screen the unmatched paid providers for the outsourcing test so goods-only suppliers are not counted as gaps.
Treat every remaining unmatched service provider as a completeness exception before sampling.
testing.done: the three-way reconciliation is complete and every unmatched service provider is logged as a completeness exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of material arrangements and 100% of ICT providers with privileged access to firm systems.
Take 20 further entries at random with a recorded seed from the non-material population, weighted to those supporting important business services.
Take 100% of arrangements signed or reclassified in the period.
Record the seed, the population sizes and the extract date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all material and privileged-access arrangements and all new arrangements is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the outsourcing and materiality classification
actions: For each sampled arrangement, read the contract scope and the service description and apply the outsourcing test independently before reading the recorded classification.
Apply the materiality decision tree from first principles using the supported important business service and its impact tolerance.
Compare to the recorded classification and treat any downgrade from material that cannot be evidenced as an exception.
Check that a material classification triggered CRO approval and a PRA pre-notification, and that a non-material call on an ICT provider with privileged access was explicitly justified.
testing.done: each sampled classification is independently re-performed and every difference from the recorded classification is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the PRA pre-notification lead time
actions: For every material arrangement entered or materially changed in the period, take the notification send date from the sent correspondence and the contract execution date from the signature page.
Compute the elapsed period and compare it to the 6-week expectation, recording the shortfall in days where it is short.
Confirm the notification described the service, the provider, the countries and the supported important business services rather than being a bare notice.
Any material arrangement entered with under 6 weeks of notice, or none, is a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every material arrangement has a recomputed notification lead time against the 6-week expectation with shortfalls quantified in days.

testing.step: Test contract clause coverage against the executed document
actions: For each sampled material arrangement, open the executed contract and locate each mandatory clause at the section reference recorded on the checklist.
Confirm the clause as executed says what the checklist claims — an audit clause limited to the provider's own summary report is not a firm and regulator access right.
Check sub-outsourcing consent, data location, security incident notification timescale, continuity testing participation, termination and exit assistance specifically.
Log every clause absent, materially narrower than the standard, or amended by a side letter as an exception.
testing.done: each mandatory clause is located and read in the executed contract, and narrowed or absent clauses are logged.

testing.step: Trace monitoring, assurance and exit evidence
actions: For each sampled material arrangement confirm a service level report exists within the contractual reporting frequency and that actual performance is recorded, not just received.
Confirm the provider's most recent independent assurance report is on file, is dated within the last twelve months and that the complementary controls it names are assigned to a firm owner.
Confirm an exit plan exists, was reviewed within the last twelve months and names an actual alternative provider or in-house route.
Log stale assurance reports, unassigned complementary controls and exit plans with no named alternative as exceptions.
testing.done: each sampled material arrangement evidences current monitoring, a current assurance report with owned complementary controls and a reviewed exit plan.

testing.step: Test the register against the continuity dependency maps and the CMDB
actions: Take the third-party dependencies recorded on the important business service dependency maps and check each has a register entry.
Take the ICT providers on the register and check each maps to live CMDB configuration items and to a third-party account list in the identity platform.
List providers on the dependency maps but not the register, and providers on the register with no CMDB linkage.
Log privileged third-party accounts with no register entry as a significant exception to the Chief Info Security Officer.
testing.done: the register, the dependency maps and the CMDB reconcile, with privileged accounts lacking a register entry escalated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the provider, the arrangement, the field or clause and the difference found.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: arrangement never registered, materiality downgraded without evidence, notification sent late or not at all, clause narrowed at negotiation, assurance report stale, exit plan generic, CMDB linkage missing.
Name an owner and a remediation date and require the register entry or contract amendment as evidence rather than an action plan.
Escalate missed pre-notifications to the Chief Risk Officer and Regulatory Counsel within one business day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue id, a named root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an evidence requirement.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the register completeness rate from the three-way reconciliation, the notification compliance rate and the clause coverage rate on material arrangements.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective against the compliance function duty in Conditions Governing Business 4 and the outsourcing register expectation.
Have the reviewer — who owns no register relationship and sits outside procurement and vendor management — sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, every missed pre-notification and every concentration risk outside appetite to the board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating completeness, notification and clause coverage rates with a conclusion is filed and reported to the Risk Committee.
